data.title: The great displacement is already well underway?
data.author: JSLegendDev
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大龄技术人员在就业市场中面临的挑战及应对策略，特别是在AI和经济变化的背景下。

不同观点：
• **改名策略**：[hackingonempty] 建议改用更常见的名字如"Shawn Kay"来避免因名字特别而被淘汰，等到HR流程时再使用 legal name。这个建议基于名字可能带来的潜在偏见。

• **经济与社会变化**：[Havoc] 认为就业困难不仅仅是AI取代岗位的问题，而是整体经济环境变化的结果，尤其是零利率政策的结束导致很多公司不再招聘。

• **地域与行业建议**：[ecshafer] 建议专注于学习C, C++, Java，并在当地寻找工作机会，尤其是在国防行业，而非只关注web开发工作。

• **远程工作与市场竞争**：[uberman] 指出选择居住在农村地区和坚持远程工作可能增加了就业难度，建议重新发布AI相关内容以吸引关注。

• **自主创业与技能转型**：[dexterlagan] 分享个人经验，建议从为他人工作转向自主创业和实现个人想法，以应对就业市场的变化。

• **技能与市场需求匹配**：[speedbird] 强调需要调整自己以符合市场需求，包括可能接受薪资下降或工作条件的变化，并建议与业内信任的人讨论。

• **国际对比与职业选择**：[Padriac] 提到在澳大利亚，军事技术岗位待遇优厚且正在招聘，建议考虑相关职业。

• **技术过时问题**：[Arnt] 指出只会单一语言如PHP的开发人员面临过时风险，类似于多年前的Perl开发者。

补充讨论：
• **系统脆弱性与经济转型**：[RainyDayTmrw] 和 [tetris11] 讨论了当前社会和经济系统的脆弱性，以及经济转型过程中可能出现的失业问题和应对策略。

• **同理心与评论动机**：[1attice] 提醒评论者在发表意见时要保持同理心，并反思自己评论的动机和潜在的心理防御机制。

• **政策与社会支持**：[adamc] 提到当前缺乏有效的社会支持和政策解决方案，对未来感到担忧。

争议焦点：
• 就业市场变化的主要原因：是AI取代岗位还是整体经济环境的变化。
• 改名策略的有效性和伦理问题：是否应通过改名来规避偏见。
• 远程工作的可行性与市场竞争力：在当前环境下是否应坚持远程工作。

data.title: Air Traffic Control
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了空中交通管制的历史和发展，特别关注其技术、管理和社交方面的复杂性。文章指出，空中交通管制的衰退源于数十年的投资不足、国防工业体系的掌控、联邦航空管理局的管理不善以及里根镇压PATCO罢工的长期影响。文章回顾了早期航空时代，由于飞机数量少且技术有限，空中交通管制需求不高，主要通过旗帜和信号灯指挥飞机降落。第一次世界大战推动了航空无线电的发展，使得地面控制成为可能。战后，民用航空迅速发展，商业航空公司开始使用无线电进行调度和天气咨询，邮政部门的航空邮件服务也为现代民航奠定了基础。邮政合同不仅资助了航空业，还促成了多家大型航空公司的成长。

主要讨论点：空中交通管制（ATC）系统的演变、现状及其现代化需求

不同观点：
• [ilamont] 对国际航班在欧洲和加勒比地区国家之间的交接流程感到好奇，关注空中交通控制系统在边境较小国家之间的运作方式。
• [_whiteCaps_] 提到二战时期的战术空军通过无线电与陆军协调攻击敌方目标，但对具体操作方式（如是否通过中央调度员）表示不确定。
• [ranger207] 讨论了海军战术数据系统（NTDS）与空军SAGE系统的相似性，指出NTDS主要是军事用途，且其技术发展对民用社会影响较小，同时推荐了一些参考资料。
• [telotortium] 关注博客的用户体验，建议增加关闭背景图像的选项，以提高阅读体验。
• [kristel100] 感慨空中交通管制系统的复杂性和其对日常生活的隐形支持，强调其在现代社会中的重要性。
• [jillesvangurp] 认为当前ATC系统效率低下、可扩展性差，且存在安全隐患，建议通过现代化技术（如数字化通信、安全认证等）减少人为语音交流，提升系统自动化和安全性。他还指出，未来电池电动飞机和自主飞行器的发展将大幅增加空中交通量，现有系统难以应对这一增长，亟需技术变革。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于当前ATC系统是否能够适应未来航空交通量的增长以及技术进步的需求。
• [jillesvangurp] 强调了现代技术（如数字通信、安全认证）在提升ATC效率和安全性方面的潜力，并指出当前系统在应对未来交通量增长方面的不足。
• 对历史系统的回顾（如NTDS和SAGE）提供了对现有系统演变过程的了解，并为现代化讨论提供了背景支持。
• 用户体验问题（如博客背景图像）虽然不直接相关，但也反映了技术系统中用户需求的多样性。

>>> 2025-05-11 air traffic control (
PDF
)
Air traffic control has been in the news lately, on account of my country's
declining ability to do it. Well, that's a long-term trend, resulting from
decades of under-investment, severe capture by our increasingly incompetent
defense-industrial complex, no small degree of management incompetence in the
FAA, and long-lasting effects of Reagan crushing the PATCO strike. But that's
just my opinion, you know, maybe airplanes got too woke. In any case, it's an
interesting time to consider how
weird
parts of air traffic control are. The
technical, administrative, and social aspects of ATC all seem two notches more
complicated than you would expect. ATC is heavily influenced by its peculiar
and often accidental development, a product of necessity that perpetually
trails behind the need, and a beneficiary of hand-me-down military practices
and technology.
Aviation Radio
In the early days of aviation, there was little need for ATC---there just
weren't many planes, and technology didn't allow ground-based controllers to do
much of value. There was some use of flags and signal lights to clear aircraft
to land, but for the most part ATC had to wait for the development of aviation
radio. The impetus for that work came mostly from the First World War.
Here we have to note that the history of aviation is very closely intertwined
with the history of warfare. Aviation technology has always rapidly advanced
during major conflicts, and as we will see, ATC is no exception.
By 1913, the US Army Signal Corps was experimenting with the use of radio to
communicate with aircraft. This was pretty early in radio technology, and the
aircraft radios were huge and awkward to operate, but it was also early in
aviation and "huge and awkward to operate" could be similarly applied to the
aircraft of the day. Even so, radio had obvious potential in aviation. The
first military application for aircraft  was reconnaissance. Pilots could fly
past the front to find artillery positions and otherwise provide useful
information, and then return with maps. Well, even better than returning with a
map was providing the information in real-time, and by the end of the war
medium-frequency AM radios were well developed for aircraft.
Radios in aircraft lead naturally to another wartime innovation: ground
control. Military personnel on the ground used radio to coordinate the
schedules and routes of reconnaissance planes, and later to inform on the
positions of fighters and other enemy assets. Without any real way to know
where the planes were, this was all pretty primitive, but it set the basic
pattern that people on the ground could keep track of aircraft and provide
useful information.
Post-war, civil aviation rapidly advanced. The early 1920s saw numerous
commercial airlines adopting radio, mostly for business purposes like schedule
coordination. Once you were in contact with someone on the ground, though, it
was only logical to ask about weather and conditions. Many of our modern
practices like weather briefings, flight plans, and route clearances originated
as more or less formal practices within individual airlines.
Air Mail
The government was not left out of the action. The Post Office operated what
may have been the largest commercial aviation operation in the world during the
early 1920s, in the form of Air Mail. The Post Office itself did not have any
aircraft; all of the flying was contracted out---initially to the Army Air
Service, and later to a long list of regional airlines. Air Mail was considered
a high priority by the Post Office and proved very popular with the public.
When the transcontinental route began proper operation in 1920, it became
possible to get a letter from New York City to San Francisco in just 33 hours
by transferring it between airplanes in a nearly non-stop relay race.
The Post Office's largesse in contracting the service to private operators
provided not only the funding but the very motivation for much of our modern
aviation industry. Air travel was not very popular at the time, being loud and
uncomfortable, but the mail didn't complain. The many contract mail carriers of
the 1920s grew and consolidated into what are now some of the United States'
largest companies. For around a decade, the Post Office almost singlehandedly
bankrolled civil aviation, and passengers were a side hustle [1].
Air mail ambition was not only of economic benefit. Air mail routes were often
longer and more challenging than commercial passenger routes. Transcontinental
service required regular flights through sparsely populated parts of the
interior, challenging the navigation technology of the time and making rescue
of downed pilots a major concern. Notably, air mail operators did far more
nighttime flying than any other commercial aviation in the 1920s. The post
office became the government's de facto technical leader in civil aviation.

data.title: Understanding LucasArts' iMUSE System
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章（或页面）内容简短，提到与"meshula"和"LabMidi"相关的项目。页面显示项目是公开的，但需要登录才能更改通知设置。当前项目有4次被 fork，并获得了54个星标（Star）。文章主要是关于一个代码库或项目的简要状态信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iMUSE系统的特点、应用及其在游戏音乐中的影响

不同观点：
• [kjander79] 认为iMUSE系统的无缝音乐过渡非常出色，比如在《X-Wing》中，当帝国战舰出现时，音乐会自然切换到《帝国进行曲》。然而，他也指出基于CD音频的游戏在音乐切换时显得生硬，并质疑这是否是系统本身的局限性。他还提出，现代技术可以通过虚拟MIDI系统实现类似效果。

• [gmueckl] 强调了创造适用于iMUSE系统的内容的工具和过程的重要性，认为技术系统对创意人员的友好性是一个重大挑战。他表示，LucasArts在这方面做得很好，并对创作过程表示好奇。

• [riotnrrd] 分享了与iMUSE开发者Nick共事的个人经历，称赞其为人与专业能力，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• [jesusgm] 通过对比《Monkey Island》两代游戏的音乐体验，突出了iMUSE系统在游戏沉浸感方面的提升，强调实际体验的重要性。

• [Dwedit] 提到《Banjo-Kazooie》使用了简单的动态音乐实现方法，通过额外音轨的淡入淡出实现动态音乐，指出这种方法虽然简单但常用。

• [i_v] 探讨了音乐制作作为游戏引擎一部分的长期兴趣，提到了《Elder Scrolls Online》和AI生成音乐的例子，思考这种技术在游戏叙事和互动中的未来潜力。

补充讨论：
• [Lightkey] 提到了ScummVM与iMUSE相关的法律问题，指出iMUSE曾拥有专利，ScummVM团队需小心处理。同时，对开发者Nick认可非官方实现表示赞赏。

争议焦点：
• iMUSE系统在CD音频游戏中的局限性及其是否为技术限制所致，是[kjander79]提出的主要争议点。
• 动态音乐实现的复杂性与简单方法之间的对比，是[Dwedit]和[kjander79]讨论的一个潜在争议点。

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了科学研究中的“P值操纵”（P hacking）问题，即通过调整分析或数据以获得统计显著结果的不当行为。这种做法可能源于研究者过早查看数据、重复实验直到获得显著结果、选择性报告有利数据等。文章列举了五种常见的P值操纵形式，包括过早结束实验、重复实验直到获得显著结果、挑选有利数据、调整数据以获得显著性等。P值操纵会导致科学结果的不可重复性和不可复制性，破坏科学研究的可靠性。文章建议研究者应事先确定样本量和数据处理规则，并如实报告所有实验结果，以维护科学诚信。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：P-hacking问题及其在科学研究中的表现和影响

不同观点：
• parpfish认为，P-hacking有时并非出于恶意，而是由于对新统计方法的探索和旧数据集的再分析引发的。他们提到，研究人员可能因为使用新方法从旧数据中找到“显著效果”而受到鼓励去发表结果，而不是进行验证性实验。
• gwerbret指出，在临床试验中，提前停止实验并不一定是P-hacking，特别是在早期证据显示明显效果或无效时。他们认为，这种做法可以节省时间和资源，并举了关于 circumcision 和HIV感染的临床试验为例。
• neilv用赌徒的比喻说明，反复进行实验可能最终会得到偶然的显著结果，强调需要在实验结束后再进行结果分析。
• cypherpunks01引用了一句改编的谚语，暗示研究人员的职业发展可能依赖于P-hacking，因此很难停止这种行为。
• zipy124强调了Bonferroni修正的重要性，指出许多论文没有对多重比较进行校正，导致结果不可靠。
• p4ul支持透明度，并建议改变 tenure 和 promotion 的激励机制，使可重复性成为评估的重要因素。
• dimal认为，停止P-hacking可能会在短期内影响职业发展，因为发表负面结果可能不利于职业生涯，但长期风险可以通过发表不重要的研究来减轻。
• eviks指出文章的讽刺性，认为遵循文章的建议可能不利于职业发展。
• andrewla提到预注册（preregistration）是解决P-hacking问题的一部分，并建议这种做法需要有“牙齿”，即如果研究被撤回，应该影响研究者的声誉。
• pizlonator提到软件优化中类似P-hacking的行为，认为需要通过良好的性能置信区间（perf CI）来防御，但承认统计学上的自我欺骗是难以完全避免的。
• gregwebs认为文章揭示了科学界对再现性问题的无知，感到非常不安。
• smallmancontrov指出“狗屎null假设”是常见的P-hacking策略，这种假设容易被拒绝，且常常在同行评审中被忽视。
• WhitneyLand对文章需要解释基本伦理和常识感到尴尬，认为这是科学界自我伤害的一部分，导致公众对科学的信任丧失。

补充讨论：
• spinf97提问如何决定实验的重复次数，这涉及到实验设计和统计功效的考虑，是解决P-hacking问题的一个实际操作问题。

争议焦点：
• P-hacking的定义和其合理性的边界。例如，gwerbret和parpfish认为在某些情况下，提前停止实验或使用新方法分析数据不一定是P-hacking，而其他评论者如neilv和cypherpunks01则强调这种做法的潜在危害和道德问题。
• 科学界的激励机制是否助长了P-hacking。p4ul和dimal提到职业发展和发表压力对P-hacking的影响，而andrewla建议通过预注册和声誉风险来改变这种现状。

It can happen so easily. You’re excited about an experiment, so you sneak an early peek at the data to see if the
P
value — a measure of statistical significance — has dipped below the threshold of 0.05. Or maybe you’ve tried analysing your results in several different ways, hoping one will give you that significant finding. These temptations are common, especially in the cut-throat world of publish-or-perish academia. But giving in to them can lead to what scientists call
P
hacking.
P
hacking is the practice of tweaking the analysis or data to get a statistically significant result. In other words, you’re fishing for a desirable outcome and reporting only the catches, while ignoring all the times you came up empty. It might get you a publication in the short term, but
P
hacking contributes to the reproducibility and replicability crisis in science by filling the literature with dubious or unfounded conclusions.
Most researchers don’t set out to cheat, but they could unknowingly make choices that push them towards a significant result. Here are five ways
P
hacking can slip into your research.
Ending the experiment too early
You might plan to gather 30 samples but find yourself running a quick analysis halfway through, just to see where things stand. If you notice a statistically significant difference after 15 samples, you might be inclined to stop the experiment early — after all, you’ve found what you were looking for.
It’s time to talk about ditching statistical significance
But stopping an experiment once you find a significant effect but before you reach your predetermined sample size is classic
P
hacking. It’s like declaring the winner of an election after polling just half the electorate: the result might not be representative of reality. What’s the solution? Decide on the sample size or data-collection process ahead of time and stick to it, no matter how eager you are to see the results.
Running experiments until you get a hit
Another often-unintentional form of
P
hacking is repeating the experiment or analysis until you obtain a statistically significant result. Imagine you run an experiment and the outcome is insignificant. You try again with a new batch of samples — still nothing. You repeat the study once more, and
voila
!
P
< 0.05. Success? Not quite. If you selectively report only the attempt that ‘worked’ and ignore those that didn’t, you’re engaging in
P
hacking by omission. As any gambler knows, if you roll the dice often enough, eventually you’ll get the result you want by chance alone (not that I’m a gambler). The better approach is to report all the experimental replicates, including those that didn’t work.
Cherry-picking your results
A less benign form of
P
hacking is selective reporting. Imagine you measure several outcomes or observe your effect at multiple time points — for instance, testing a therapy’s impact on recipients’ blood pressure, cholesterol, weight and blood sugar regularly over an entire month. After analysing the data, you find that only one outcome — say, blood sugar at week 3 — showed a significant improvement. You might be tempted to highlight this one promising result and downplay the rest, or even omit them from your report. This is cherry-picking: by showing only the favourable data and ignoring everything else, you create a biased narrative.
In this example, people might think the therapy worked because it lowered blood sugar at week 3, even though the overall data are not so rosy. Putting these data into the paper’s supplementary material and continuing with the experiment on the basis of this one finding is also a no-no. You should report all relevant results, not just the ones that support the hypothesis. Science progresses faster when we know what doesn’t work, as well as what does.
Tweaking your data
In data analysis, you often have to make judgements about what to include, what to exclude and how to report the data.
P
hacking can sneak in when those decisions are guided by the desire to achieve significance rather than by scientific reasoning. For example, you might notice an outlier in your data set. Including it in the analysis gives you a
P
value of 0.08, whereas excluding it brings
P
down to 0.03. Problem solved? Not quite.
In these cases, it is best practice to go back to the original data or laboratory notes to determine whether experimental conditions could explain this outlier. Perhaps you pipetted double the amount of reagent into your sample, or construction work nearby during the time you were testing that animal affected its behaviour. Researchers can often rationalize their data-filtration decisions, and most of those decisions are warranted. But if the real motive is to turn an insignificant result into a significant one, it crosses into questionable territory. The key is to decide on data-filtering rules before looking at the results. data.title: Open Hardware Ethernet Switch project, part 1
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者长期开发的开源硬件以太网交换机项目，该项目推动了其他如ngscopeclient和高速度探测器等项目的发展。文章回顾了项目的历史和进展，最早的尝试是2012年左右使用FPGA设计的“open-gig-switch”，但由于技术限制和设备不足，该设计未能成功。在随后的几年中，作者通过攻读博士学位和后续工作积累了更多经验，并购买了更先进的设备如350 MHz示波器。为了解决高速信号完整性问题，作者还设计了未完成的10 GHz采样示波器FREESAMPLE，并开发了高带宽探测器和多个协议解码器。最终，作者规划了LATENTx系列网络设备的发展蓝图，其中LATENTPINK将作为原型/技术演示平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源网络硬件项目的进展、挑战及技术选择

不同观点：
• Aurornis认为该项目非常 impressive，但担心项目范围不断扩大（scope creep）会影响实际成果的完成。他希望看到更简单、可开放迭代的设计，如4端口交换机，并对项目中的其他未兑现产品表示关注。
• Transpute提到NetFPGA项目，认为这是另一个在学术和研究环境中使用的开放网络平台，指出了其全球应用的广泛性。
• Purpleidea表示希望项目能支持switchdev，认为主流交换功能与常规Linux网络的无缝集成将带来积极影响，并强调减少专有接口的重要性。
• Bgnn从自身经验出发，讨论了以太网PHY的设计，并对是否能以较低数量购买10G或25G的PHY表示关注。
• Acyou对从不可靠来源购买网络硬件表示担忧，尤其是可能存在后门的风险，并指出开放源代码硬件在安全性方面的挑战。
• Zokier建议考虑使用Microchip的Sparx-5交换机ASIC，认为这是一个具有Linux支持且价格合理的选择，但同时也理解自定义交换引擎的吸引力。
• Westurner提供了关于OpenWRT支持的48+2端口交换机的信息，并详细讨论了与项目相关的各种开源资源和技术细节。
• Kristel100对DIY网络设备的冷却和功耗问题表示关注，认为这是此类项目成功的关键因素。

补充讨论：
• 项目范围扩大（scope creep）是讨论中的一个重要问题，Aurornis和Westurner都提到了项目复杂性和实际成果之间的平衡。
• 安全性是一个争议焦点，Acyou对从不可靠来源购买硬件的担忧引发了对开放源代码硬件安全性的讨论。
• 对具体技术选择（如PHY类型、ASIC型号）的讨论反映了参与者对技术实现细节的关注。
• 开放源代码硬件项目的实际应用和支持情况（如NetFPGA和OpenWRT）也是讨论的重要内容，提供了其他类似项目的参考。
• 项目的实际可行性和持续性（如产品可靠性和冷却问题）被认为是需要关注的重要方面。

通过这些观点，可以看出参与者们对开源网络硬件项目的热情，同时也关注其实际可行性、技术细节和潜在的安全风险。

43934869.article_content:
Switch project, part 1
2025-05-08 18:00
One of my longest-running projects has been an open hardware Ethernet switch. This has been one of the key driving forces behind many of my other projects, such as ngscopeclient and the high speed probes. It was also the project that got me into high speed digital design.
So I figured itâs time to kick off a series with a short writeup of where things are now, how we got there, and whatâs coming next. If you follow me on Mastodon youâve probably seen most of this in bits and pieces but I wanted to collect it all in one place.
Ancient history: The first switch
The first generation never had a name, it was just called âopen-gig-switchâ or something in my subversion repository (this was circa 2012 before I was primarily running on git).
I couldnât find any many-port gigabit switch ASICs that were suitable for an OSH project (i.e. purchasable in qty 1, no NDA needed for datasheet, etc). So an FPGA-based from-scratch design seemed the only option.
This board pushed a lot of limits for meâ¦ my first use of switching power supplies rather than LDOs, my biggest and most complex board to date, and I think maybe even my first use of an RGMII PHY (I had previously used the Microchip ENC424J600 which is a full 10/100 Ethernet MAC + PHY including buffer memory attached to a parallel bus or SPI interface).
And at the time my fanciest piece of test equipment was a 100 MHz Rigol DS1102D. So I had no way to do signal integrity measurements on either the Ethernet differential pairs or even the 250 MT/s RGMII lines.
This one never really got anywhere. I got three of the four PHYs up and running, PHY #4 never worked (I canât remember if it wouldnât link up, wouldnât pass data, or what). I tried resoldering a bunch of stuff but never got it functional.
I tried to bring up a basic switch with only 3 ports, but very quickly realized that 15K LUTs, <1 Mbit of BRAM, and no external CPU would make that very challenging. The XC6SLX25 was not a large FPGA and adding the Xilinx DDR controller and a softcore CPU and three MACs didnât leave much space at all for fabric. Plus I was still a relative novice to FPGA development and wasnât quite at the point of being ready to tackle the project.
So this board ended up a dead-end, but set the stage for what was coming.
The interim years
The first switch fiasco showed me I needed more skills, better test equipment, better debug tools, and more.
I was still in grad school with little budget for equipment, but over the course of my Ph.D I became a much more experienced RTL engineer. I built a couple of boards with Ethernet that mostly worked.
But since I couldnât afford a better scope and had no way to validate SI on faster stuff, I decided to table the switch project for a bit.
In 2015 I graduated and got a job that paid much more than I was making as a graduate teaching assistant. One of my first purchases was my first ârealâ oscilloscope, a 350 MHz Teledyne LeCroy WaveSurfer 3034. This was actually fast enough to do SI work on RGMII and protocol-decode 100baseTX, but I dreamed of much faster.
I knew I wanted to put 10GbE on the switch whenever I finally got back to it, and didnât expect to be able to afford a many-GHz scope any time soon, so I started looking at alternative approaches to validate SI at these speeds. This led me down another path of yak shaving in which I started designing a 10 GHz sampling oscilloscope named FREESAMPLE (which never got finished, but I do want to revisit the project one day). This, then, got put on ice when I realized a high speed scope would be useless without an equally high bandwidth probe to feed it with.
You probably already know where this story goes. My open hardware 16 GHz probe (which probably deserves a post or series of its own) is now essentially done and ramping up an initial PVT run, hopefully I can actually make them in quantity and offer to the public in the coming months.
Over the course of shaving these yaks I also bought a house, took a year or two off major projects to refurbish it, got a Sonnet EM solver seat, found a shockingly affordably 16 GHz oscilloscope on eBay (which made FREESAMPLE much less of a priority), rewrote âscopeclientâ with OpenGL acceleration as âglscopeclientâ, then rewrote it again in Vulkan as ângscopeclientâ. I also created protocol decodes for 10/100 baseTX, 1000baseX, SGMII, QSGMII, 10Gbase-R, and a few other potentially relevant protocols.
I also started dreaming up a roadmap for a whole family of networking equipment under the randomly generated umbrella name LATENTx, using colors for sub-projects (vaguely inspired by the Lockheed HAVE BLUE). The original roadmap called for LATENTRED to be a gigabit edge switch and LATENTORANGE to be a 10G core switch, but I decided that a prototyping/technology demonstrator platform was called for first. LATENTINFRARED was too long so I went with LATENTPINK as the name.

• 安全性是一个争议焦点，Acyou对从不可靠来源购买硬件的担忧引发了对开放源代码硬件安全性的讨论。
• 对具体技术选择（如PHY类型、ASIC型号）的讨论反映了参与者对技术实现细节的关注。
• 开放源代码硬件项目的实际应用和支持情况（如NetFPGA和OpenWRT）也是讨论的重要内容，提供了其他类似项目的参考。
• 项目的实际可行性和持续性（如产品可靠性和冷却问题）被认为是需要关注的重要方面。

通过这些观点，可以看出参与者们对开源网络硬件项目的热情，同时也关注其实际可行性、技术细节和潜在的安全风险。

data.author: pekim
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在计算机使用上的一些独特习惯，这些习惯体现了一种“短暂性策略”（Policy of transience）。主要包括：关闭持久的shell历史记录、定期清理GUI桌面、频繁关闭整个网页浏览器、关闭X11会话管理，以及使用tmpfs作为临时工作空间。作者并非试图说服他人采纳这些习惯，而是分享自己的做法。他关闭shell历史记录的动机源于对隐私的担忧，尽管没有具体的安全问题，但他对系统长期保存操作记录感到不安。这种短暂性策略还涉及其他实践，如定期删除电子邮件和自动化操作系统设置。作者强调，这些做法适合个人选择，不一定适用于所有人。

• **dgunay的观点**：默认不删除数据，所有重要数据都会自动备份到设备外。他提到见过许多人因为无法从旧设备中恢复数据而感到困扰，因此自己的策略是确保任何时候丢失设备都不会导致数据丢失，包括使用Git时也会及时提交和推送更改。

• **AstralStorm的观点**：认为缺乏会话管理和持久性会导致效率低下，即使是像Tails这样安全的系统也有持久性选项。他指出，真正的持久性在于将脚本和高级内容备份到适当的存档中，并加以标记，但目前缺乏一个有效的平台来减少不必要的努力。

补充讨论：
• 数据保存的策略在不同用户之间存在较大差异，主要争议点在于数据的临时性与永久性保存之间的平衡。

• 存储成本和数据价值之间的权衡，特别是在长时间保存数据的情况下，也是讨论的一个重要方面（spacerzasp和hinkley的观点）。

Policy of transience
[Simon Tatham, 2025-05-09]
Introduction
The habits
Turn off persistent shell history
Clear my GUI desktop regularly
Close my entire web browser frequently
Turn off X11 session management
Use a tmpfs on
~/mem
as my main scratch
space
Policy of transience
Other related practices
Corporate records management: scheduled deletion of email
Automated operating system setup from a recipe
Exceptions to the policy
Conclusion
Introduction
I have several habits in my computer usage which are unusual by
many peopleâs standards (although some more so than others), and
which all kind of point in the same direction.
At the time I adopted each one, I didnât recognise this. Each
habit seemed desirable in its own context for one reason or
another, but it wasnât a lot later until I spotted the common
theme running through them all. The theme wasnât always the
reason I adopted the habit in the first place â but I think itâs
the reason Iâve
kept
all these habits, after trying
them out for some other reason.
In this article Iâll describe the habits Iâm thinking of, and
the more general idea that theyâre all instances of, which I now
think of as a âpolicy of transienceâ.
Iâm not trying to persuade anyone else that they should adopt
this general policy, or even any of the specific habits. I just
put the ideas out here in case theyâre of interest, for people
to consider, and decide
whether
theyâd find any or all
of it useful. If any of this is useful to you, great â and if
you decide itâs not for you, thatâs fine too.
The habits
Hereâs a list of the habits that I now classify under the
general heading of âpolicy of transienceâ. I
think
these are in roughly chronological order of me adopting them,
though itâs hard to be sure.
Turn off persistent shell history
I use the Linux command line, specifically
bash
.
Like many other modern Unix shells,
bash
keeps a
history of the commands youâve typed, so that you can recall
them and run them again, or modify a previous one slightly to do
a new thing.
This can be used in the immediate short term: type a command,
it doesnât quite work, recall it and edit one typo, try again.
But it can also be useful over the long term: recall a command
you ran last week, or last year, or that thing you do about once
a month. To support the long-term uses of this
feature,
bash
saves your shell history to a file
when you exit the shell (by
default
~/.bash_history
), and reloads that file
when it starts up. So you can still recall a command even if
youâve logged out or rebooted the whole machine since running
it.
Many people find this persistent history feature very useful,
and go to some lengths to improve it further â you can configure
a larger number of stored commands, some shells will sync their
history constantly instead of just on exit, there are plugins to
help you search it more easily, and so on. The general view
seems to be: shell history is good, more and easier-to-use
history is even better.
But I go the opposite way. My unusual habit is:
turn
off the history file completely
, by putting the command
â
unset HISTFILE
â in my
.bashrc
. I
still get history within a single instance of the shell, so I
can edit my last command ten times until it works properly; but
history isnât shared between my terminal windows, or preserved
when I log out and log in again.
All
the shell history
I allow myself is localised and short-term.
I started doing this very early in my Linux-using career, very
soon after I found out the history file existed in the first
place. I think my initial motivation was an extremely vague
privacy concern: it just felt
creepy
that my shell
would be remembering that much detail about stuff Iâd done in
the past.
There are certainly valid
specific
privacy concerns
about shell history. Sometimes you write an actual secret, such
as a password, on a command line by mistake. (Oops, had focus in
the wrong window.) And sometimes you just have to hold your nose
and put a secret on a command line on purpose, because some
badly designed tool wonât let you pass it in any other way.
(Thatâs already a danger, of course, because other users of the
system can see it in
ps
â but itâs one thing to
take that risk very briefly while the command is actually
running, and quite another to have a copy of the secret
preserved in
~/.bash_history
for months or years.)
But I donât think I had anything that specific in mind to begin
with: I just felt generically uneasy with the idea.
(Of course, if you
know
youâve just written a secret
on a command line, you can delete the command from that shellâs
history on purpose, before it gets saved to the file. But if you
did it by accident, you might not realise you need to; and if
you had to recall the command and retry it a few times, you
might not manage to clean up every instance of it.)
But after I adopted this policy, and put â
unset
HISTFILE
â in the standard snippet of
.bas

data.title: TransMLA: Multi-head latent attention is all you need
data.author: ocean_moist
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA)的方法，用于解决大型语言模型在硬件上的通信瓶颈问题。MLA通过在键值层使用低秩矩阵来压缩缓存的 latent 状态，减少缓存大小，从而加快推理速度。同时，MLA利用上投影矩阵增加表达能力，以少量计算换取通信开销的降低。文章证明了Group Query Attention (GQA)可以被MLA表示，但反之不成立，并提出了转换方法TransMLA，将GQA预训练模型转为MLA模型，转换后可进一步训练以增强表达能力而不增加缓存大小。此外，文章计划开发MLA特定的推理加速技术，以保持低延迟并更高效地提取Deepseek R1模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Transformer模型中的注意力机制优化，尤其是关于多头注意力（MHA）和多查询注意力（MQA）的改进以及内存优化

不同观点：
• jbellis认为，这种新方法通过仅存储中间潜在表示来大幅减少KV缓存的大小，对于内存受限的环境（如本地推理）是一个很大的优势。具体而言，传统的多头注意力需要缓存大小为T x (nh · dh)的键和值矩阵，而新方法通过低维中间表示大大减少了存储需求。

• karmakaze分享了一个视频资源，解释了MHA、MQA、GQA和MLA，并指出DeepSeek的MLA效率提高了57倍，为讨论提供了额外的背景信息和可视化解释。

• killerstorm提到了一篇相关的论文，该论文讨论了将注意力蒸馏到类似RWKV模型的更激进方法，提供了另一种优化思路。

• octocop对标题表示不满，认为不应夸大宣传，指出之前的类似方法并未达到预期。

• olq_plo对新模型在Hugging Face（HF）上的发布表示期待。

• wiz21c询问了mamba模型的进展，并自行找到了相关讨论链接，展示了社区内的其他讨论资源。

• magicalhippo从旁观者的角度分析了新模型的优势，特别提到了新模型在增加表达能力的同时仅增加了约10%的内存使用，并可以通过微调将现有GQA模型转换为新模型。此外，还详细解释了低秩近似（low-rank approximation）的原理及其在内存节省和表达能力提升方面的作用。

• kavalg给出了一个简化的总结，认为TransMLA是一种压缩已训练GQA模型的方法，并可进一步微调以加速推理。

• EGreg对标题表示反感，认为不应使用夸张的标题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个相关技术和方法，如低秩近似（LoRA）、Group Query Attention（GQA）、Multi-Query Attention（MQA）等，展示了当前领域内的多样化研究方向。

• 争议的焦点主要在于对新方法的宣传和命名上，部分评论者对标题和宣传方式表示不满，认为不应夸大其词。

• 讨论中还提供了多个外部资源链接，如视频解释和相关讨论链接，为深入了解提供了参考。

Title:
TransMLA: Multi-Head Latent Attention Is All You Need
Authors:
Fanxu Meng
,
Zengwei Yao
,
Muhan Zhang
View a PDF of the paper titled TransMLA: Multi-Head Latent Attention Is All You Need, by Fanxu Meng and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Modern large language models (LLMs) often encounter communication bottlenecks on current hardware, rather than purely computational constraints. Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) tackles this challenge by using low-rank matrices in the key-value (KV) layers, thereby allowing compressed latent KV states to be cached. This approach significantly reduces the KV cache size relative to traditional multi-head attention, leading to faster inference. Moreover, MLA employs an up-projection matrix to increase expressiveness, trading additional computation for reduced communication overhead. Although MLA has demonstrated efficiency and effectiveness in Deepseek V2/V3/R1, many major model providers still rely on Group Query Attention (GQA) and have not announced any plans to adopt MLA. In this paper, we show that GQA can always be represented by MLA while maintaining the same KV cache overhead, but the converse does not hold. To encourage broader use of MLA, we introduce TransMLA, a post-training method that converts widely used GQA-based pre-trained models (e.g., LLaMA, Qwen, Mixtral) into MLA-based models. After conversion, the model can undergo additional training to boost expressiveness without increasing the KV cache size. Furthermore, we plan to develop MLA-specific inference acceleration techniques to preserve low latency in transformed models, thus enabling more efficient distillation of Deepseek R1.

I mentioned last time that I’ve been working on a new website for Emmy-award-winning game composer Mike Worth. He hired me to create a highly graphical design that showcases his work. Mike loves ’90s animation, particularly Disney’s Duck Tales and other animated series. He challenged me to find a way to incorporate their retro ’90s style into his design without making it a pastiche. But that wasn’t my only challenge. I also needed to achieve that ’90s feel by using up-to-the-minute code to maintain accessibility, performance, responsiveness, and semantics. Designing for Mike was like a trip back to when mainstream website design seemed more spontaneous and less governed by conventions and best practices. Some people describe these designs as “whimsical”: adjective spontaneously fanciful or playful given to whims; capricious quaint, unusual, or fantastic — Collins English Dictionary But I’m not so sure that’s entirely accurate. “Playful?” Definitely. “Fanciful?” Possibly. But “fantastic?” That depends. “Whimsy” sounds superfluous, so I call it “expressive” instead. Studying design from way back, I remembered how websites often included graphics that combined branding, content, and navigation. Pretty much every reference to web design in the ’90s — when I designed my first website — talks about Warner Brothers’ Space Jam from 1996. Warner Brothers’ Space Jam (1996) So, I’m not going to do that. Brands like Nintendo used their home pages to direct people to their content while making branded visual statements. Cheestrings combined graphics with navigation, making me wonder why we don’t see designs like this today. Goosebumps typified this approach, combining cartoon illustrations with brightly colored shapes into a functional and visually rich banner, proving that being useful doesn’t mean being boring. Left to right: Nintendo, Cheestrings, Goosebumps . In the ’90s, when I developed graphics for websites like these, I either sliced them up and put their parts in tables or used mostly forgotten image maps. A brief overview of properties and values Let’s run through a quick refresher. Image maps date all the way back to HTML 3.2, where, first, server-side maps and then client-side maps defined clickable regions over an image using map and area elements. They were popular for graphics, maps, and navigation, but their use declined with the rise of CSS, SVG, and JavaScript. adds clickable areas to a bitmap or vector image. ... That is linked to an image using the usemap attribute: Those elements can have separate href and alt attributes and can be enhanced with ARIA to improve accessibility: ... The shape attribute specifies an area’s shape. It can be a primitive circle or rect or a polygon defined by a set of absolute x and y coordinates: Despite their age, image maps still offer plenty of benefits. They’re lightweight and need (almost) no JavaScript. More on that in just a minute. They’re accessible and semantic when used with alt , ARIA, and title attributes. Despite being from a different era, even modern mobile browsers support image maps. Design by Andy Clarke, Stuff & Nonsense. Mike Worth’s website will launch in April 2025, but you can see examples from this article on CodePen. My design for Mike Worth includes several graphic navigation elements, which made me wonder if image maps might still be an appropriate solution. Image maps in action Mike wants his website to showcase his past work and the projects he’d like to do. To make this aspect of his design discoverable and fun, I created a map for people to explore by pressing on areas of the map to open modals. This map contains numbered circles, and pressing one pops up its modal. My first thought was to embed anchors into the external map SVG: This approach is problematic. Those anchors are only active when SVG is inline and don’t work with an element. But image maps work perfectly, even though specifying their coordinates can be laborious. Fortunately, plenty of tools are available, which make defining coordinates less tedious. Upload an image, choose shape types, draw the shapes, and copy the markup: ... data.title: Anti-Personnel Computing (2023)
data.author: transpute
data.article_summary: "Anti-personnel computing"是一个新术语，用于描述21世纪初主流计算的特点。它指计算设备的使用损害用户利益，而使第三方实体受益。具体来说，"anti-personnel computer"指的是一种主要用于损害用户利益、为第三方实体谋利的计算设备。该词源自“反人员地雷”（anti-personnel mine）以及“个人计算”（personal computing）和“个人电脑”（personal computer）等词，反映了技术对用户的不利影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“反个人计算”（anti-personnel computing）及其相关概念的讨论，涉及技术对用户的负面影响、隐私问题以及可能的解决方案。

不同观点：
• JohnMakin认为当前软件行业的氛围与90年代末和2000年初的互联网泡沫时期相似，当时网页上充斥着广告和恶意软件，而现在类似的现象再次出现，反映出过度追求高估值和营收的狂热可能导致崩溃。
• vanschelven引用了GNU哲学，强调保持对计算的控制，以避免被技术控制。
• fmajid和praptak对术语提出质疑和建议。fmajid认为“反个人计算”这个术语不准确，建议用“浮士德式计算”（Faustian computing）。praptak则更倾向于使用“反特性”（antifeatures）这个更精确的术语。
• Tepix指出，当前软件系统越来越难以避免对用户不利的影响，利润最大化的驱动是这种现象的根源，并提到Cory Doctorow对“恶化”（enshittification）的描述，尽管引起了广泛关注，但非盈利和去中心化服务仍未占据较大市场份额。
• pjc50认为“用户 hostile”或“hostile architecture”更适合描述那些对用户不利的系统，而“反个人”应保留用于那些真正危险的应用，比如用于识别种族的监控摄像头。
• keisborg喜欢“反个人计算”这个术语，因为它利用了负面联想来引发讨论，并提议禁止“反个人计算”。
• DonHopkins回忆了Mac电脑崩溃时的炸弹图标，以及Windows 9x的非法操作提示，这些设计曾让用户感到恐慌。
• casey2区分了“反个人计算”和“反特性”，前者包括数据收集、封闭生态系统、暗模式和不透明程序，后者指那些对用户有害或控制用户的行为。
• 6510讨论了中国和西方在数据使用上的差异，提出可以通过加密和智能使用时间和地点来保护隐私，并提出探索“反个人计算”和有用应用之间的边界，认为可能存在互利空间。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的术语争议，包括“反个人计算”、“浮士德式计算”和“反特性”，反映了人们对技术负面影响的关注和术语准确性的追求。
• 对技术系统中利润最大化驱动带来的负面影响及其解决方案的探讨，包括Cory Doctorow的“恶化”概念和加密技术的潜在应用。
• 对隐私和数据使用的不同看法，有人担心技术对个人的控制和隐私侵犯，也有人认为在某些情况下可以通过技术手段实现互利。

争议焦点：
• 术语“反个人计算”是否准确和合适，以及如何定义和区分不同类型的技术负面影响。
• 如何在技术系统中平衡利润最大化和用户利益，以及如何有效保护隐私和避免技术对用户的控制。

data.title: Odin: A programming language made for me
data.author: gingerBill
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Odin编程语言中一些源于C语言的最佳实践，包括自定义分配器、临时分配器、跟踪分配器、指定初始化器和缓存友好编程等概念。作者通过回顾2021年在Our Machinery工作时使用C语言开发游戏引擎的经历，展示了Odin如何整合这些实践并使其更强大。

1. **自定义分配器**：Odin内置了统一的分配器接口，允许动态内存分配，比C的标准库更灵活。
2. **临时分配器**：Odin提供内置的临时分配器（context.temp_allocator），用于短期内存分配，如游戏中的一帧。
3. **跟踪分配器**：用于检测内存泄漏，Odin的跟踪分配器会在程序结束时打印未释放的内存信息。
4. **零初始化（ZII）**：尽量使内存的零值在各种情况下有效。

Odin的"核心"和"基础"库作为源码随编译器分发，允许开发者根据需要自定义。这些特性使Odin成为作者心目中理想的编程语言。

不同观点：
• alphazard认为Odin是一门优秀的语言，其设计者GingerBill在语言设计中的权衡和问题解决能力非常出色。他强调了Odin在借鉴其他语言优点（如Go的标准库包结构）的同时，也有自己的创新（如上下文系统）。
• mrkeen对Odin的自动零初始化特性表示担忧，认为这可能会导致错误值在程序中传播，主张通过编译时错误或运行时崩溃来处理未初始化变量的问题。
• jongjong分享了自己编写简单查询语言的经历，强调了通过严格的空间处理来实现无需引号表示字符串的特性。
• jkercher表示Odin满足了C程序员的需求，提供了诸如标记联合、切片、动态数组、映射和自定义分配器等功能，同时具有 distinct typing、多返回值和泛型等提高编程体验的特性。

• leecommamichael分享了自己在Odin编程中的积极体验，特别是参数化多态性的良好实现。
• macintux提到Odin在Hacker News上的讨论热度。
• Quitschquat对Odin的自定义内存布局特性感兴趣，并询问是否可以创建自定义的#foo。
• jay_kyburz作为一个游戏程序员，喜欢Odin的简洁和易用性，特别是其类似脚本语言的特性。

• knowitnone反问如果C提供了Odin的特性，是否还会继续使用C，暗示C社区未能进化和改进。

• jmull认为通过C本身的改进可以解决C的问题，并指出新建语言的效率和可持续性问题，主张通过渐进式解决方案改善现有C代码。

补充讨论：

• 对C标准库的批评及其可能的改进方案。
• 对新建语言（如Odin）与传统语言（如C）在解决编程问题上的有效性比较。
• 对Odin、Zig和Jai未来竞争和发展的期待。

争议焦点：
• Odin的自动零初始化特性是否优于编译时错误或运行时崩溃的处理方式。
• 新建语言（如Odin）是否是解决C语言问题的最佳途径，还是应该通过改进C本身来实现。

Table of Contents
Custom allocators

Tracking allocators
Zero is initialized (ZII)

Finally: Simplicity
Not everyone has my programming background
Thanks for reading!
In my book
Understanding the Odin Programming Language
I wrote that “Odin incorporates some of my favorite C best practices, straight into the language”. But I didn’t really elaborate on the details. Let’s do that here!
This brings me to talking a bit about a previous job I had. Back in 2021 I worked at a place called
Our Machinery
. We were creating a whole game engine in plain C. We used a very comfortable and powerful way to program C.
We relied on concepts such as:
Custom allocators
Temporary allocators
Tracking allocators
Designated initializers
Zero is initialized
Cache friendly programming
While working there, I stumbled upon Odin. I read a bit about it. It seemed to incorporate all these things. In many ways it seemed like a language built around the specific way in which we programmed C at my job. Since I liked that way of programming, it almost seemed like a language built for me!
Custom allocators
#
At my job we had implemented our own
Allocator
interface in C. An allocator provides a custom way in which one can do dynamic memory allocations. C programmers are used to
malloc
and
free
. But you can make allocators that provide more advanced allocation strategies. Our
Allocator
interface made it possible to reason about allocators in a uniform way and pass them around to functions.
If a function accepted a parameter of type
Allocator
, then it was a hint that its return value was dynamically allocated.
This is exactly how it works in Odin. But the
Allocator
interface
is built into the language’s
base
library collection
! This meant that Odin’s
base
and
core
libraries support these allocators too. At my job, the
Allocator
interface was only supported in our own code: The C standard library didn’t support any of that. But in Odin, my own code
and
the
core
libraries can reason about custom allocators, making the concept even more powerful.
In Odin,
core
and
base
are two collections of libraries that come with the compiler. Some refer to them as the “standard library” of Odin. But they are shipped as source with the compiler. You are encouraged to make copies of the packages inside
core
, making it possible to tailor those packages to your own needs. So it’s more of a “default library” than a “standard library”. There’s a sensible default, but you’re free do things however you want.
Temporary allocators
#
Temporary memory allocators provide a way to do dynamic memory allocations that are only needed for a short while. What’s “a short while”? Video games have a very convenient “short while”: A single frame.
At my C job we had a temporary allocator that I used
a lot
. Gone was the need to manually
malloc
and
free
strings and arrays that were only needed for a short while. Just use the temp allocator. It’ll be gone the next frame! And it’s more efficient: The temp allocator allocates into pre-allocated blocks of memory.
I was happy to discover that Odin came with exactly this functionality. There’s a built in temp allocator available under the name
context.temp_allocator
. And again, the
core
libraries and my code uses the same
Allocator
interface. So I can just pass
context.temp_allocator
into any
core
library procedure that accepts an
Allocator
parameter. Whatever that procedure allocates will then be temporary. Nice!
Odin lets you choose when to clear the temp allocator. You do that by putting
free_all(context.temp_allocator)
somewhere in your code. In a video game, I’d put it as the last line of the “main game loop”.
Tracking allocators
#
Manual memory management may seem hard. How do you know if you’re leaking memory?
At my C job we had a special tracking allocator that could wrap any other allocator. It recorded when an allocation happened, and recorded when it was deallocated. That way we could display a warning on shutdown, if anything hadn’t been deallocated.
This is exactly how the tracking allocator that comes with Odin works. Just plop the code below at the top of your
main
procedure. It’ll print a list of memory leaks on shutdown.
track
:
mem
.
Tracking_Allocator
mem
.
tracking_allocator_init
(
&
track
,
context
.
allocator
)
context
.
allocator
=
mem
.
tracking_allocator
(
&
track
)
defer
{
if
len
(
track
.
allocation_map
)
>
0
{
fmt
.
eprintf
(
"=== %v allocations not freed: ===\n"
,
len
(
track
.
allocation_map
))
for
_
,
entry
in
track
.
allocation_map
{
fmt
.
eprintf
(
"- %v bytes @ %v\n"
,
entry
.
size
,
entry
.
location
)
}
}
mem
.
tracking_allocator_destroy
(
&
track
)
}
You’ll also need to do
import "core:mem"
and
import "core:fmt"
at the top of the file. The code above is from the
Odin overview
.
Zero is initialized (ZII)
#
ZII, short for zero is initialized, means that you try to make the zero-value of memory valid in as many situations as possible.
43970800.article_summary:
本文讨论了Odin编程语言中一些源于C语言的最佳实践，包括自定义分配器、临时分配器、跟踪分配器、指定初始化器和缓存友好编程等概念。作者通过回顾2021年在Our Machinery工作时使用C语言开发游戏引擎的经历，展示了Odin如何整合这些实践并使其更强大。

1. **自定义分配器**：Odin内置了统一的分配器接口，允许动态内存分配，比C的标准库更灵活。
2. **临时分配器**：Odin提供内置的临时分配器（context.temp_allocator），用于短期内存分配，如游戏中的一帧。
3. **跟踪分配器**：用于检测内存泄漏，Odin的跟踪分配器会在程序结束时打印未释放的内存信息。
4. **零初始化（ZII）**：尽量使内存的零值在各种情况下有效。

Odin的"核心"和"基础"库作为源码随编译器分发，允许开发者根据需要自定义。这些特性使Odin成为作者心目中理想的编程语言。

data.title: Alephic Writing Style Guide
data.author: otoolep
data.article_summary: 本文概述了Alephic公司的写作理念和指导原则，强调写作是实现清晰沟通和说服力的主要工具。核心写作原则包括：1.  vigor（活力）和简明，避免冗余，力求精炼；2. 使用主动语态，使句子更直接有力；3. 具体明确，用数据和实例支撑论点；4. 结构清晰，每段聚焦一个观点。此外，文章还描述了公司的声音特色：智识大胆、雄心勃勃且实际、简约而彻底，并强调语气应具对话性、深思熟虑、清晰简明且大胆。这些原则旨在保持一致的写作风格，展现专业性并与客户建立信任。

Writing
Last Updated:
May 2, 2025
Our Writing Philosophy
At Alephic, writing is our primary tool for clarity and persuasion. The written word reveals our thinking, demonstrates our expertise, and builds trust with clients. This style guide helps us maintain a consistent voice that embodies intellectual depth without sacrificing accessibility.
Core Writing Principles
1. Write with Vigor and Concision
A sentence should contain no unnecessary words, a paragraph no unnecessary sentences—just as a drawing should have no unnecessary lines and a machine no unnecessary parts.
—
Strunk & White
Say it once.
Strike any word, sentence, or paragraph that doesn't earn its keep. (If your eyes glide past a line on reread, that line's a goner.)
Move on when the point is made.
Redundancy clouds insight; brevity sharpens it.
Cut ruthlessly, then cut again.
Before you hit "publish," skim the piece at speed—whatever phrase jumps out without advancing the argument is your extra earring. Snip it.
Remember: concise doesn't mean short. Depth is welcome—every sentence just has to pay rent.
2. Use Active Voice
Lead with the doer.
Put the actor before the action: "AI transforms marketing," not "Marketing is transformed by AI."
Write subject-verb-object by default.
Active structure keeps sentences short, direct, and energetic. (Passive voice is fine when the actor is unknown
or
irrelevant—but use it knowingly, not lazily.)
Let verbs carry the load. Prefer
"We built a real-time dashboard" over "A real-time dashboard was built." Strong verbs clarify responsibility and speed understanding.
3. Be Specific and Concrete
Put a number on it.
Ground every claim in data
and
context: "U.S. bureaucracy costs ≈ $3 T—about 17% of 2016 GDP" beats "Bureaucracy is expensive."
Name your evidence.
Cite the dataset, quote the expert, and link the study. Specific sources build instant credibility.
Swap abstractions for examples.
When possible, replace "organizations often …" with a specific company, project, or metric that readers can visualize.
4. Structure for Clarity
One idea per paragraph.
Open with a topic sentence; let each paragraph advance a single step.
Signal the hierarchy.
Use clear headers (H2 → H3 → H4) so readers can skim the shape before reading the words.
Give text room to breathe.
Break dense blocks into short paragraphs and add deliberate white space.
Our Voice
Our voice balances three key qualities:
1. Intellectually Bold
We challenge conventional thinking, make unexpected connections, and offer fresh perspectives.
Do
Don't
Think from first principles
Repeat what everyone else is saying
Draw from diverse references and domains
Stay confined to marketing jargon
Connect intellectual concepts to practical applications
Pursue complexity for its own sake
Use clear frameworks to organize your thinking
Present ideas without structure
Example:
At the intersection of AI, code, and marketing expertise, we create solutions that were impossible yesterday and will be commonplace tomorrow.
2. Ambitiously Grounded
We paint visions of transformative change while keeping one foot firmly in practical reality.
Do
Don't
Acknowledge the magnitude of AI's impact
Overhype capabilities beyond what's currently possible
Focus on strategic, long-term implications
Get lost in tactical minutiae
Show the future rather than just describing it
Make claims without evidence or examples
Connect vision to practical outcomes
Float ideas without implementation paths
Example:
This is just the beginning. If these models never got better than what we have today, there would still be 10 years of runway to operationalize them.
3. Radically Simple
We present complex ideas with clarity and confidence, stripping away all unnecessary elements.
Do
Don't
Break down complex concepts into clear components
Use jargon without explanation
Present one idea at a time in logical sequence
Overload sentences with multiple concepts
Be precise and economical with language
Add unnecessary qualifiers ("very," "quite")
Read your work aloud to test for natural flow
Write in a way that sounds stilted when spoken
Example:
With AI, impossible problems become merely hard, hard problems become easy, and easy problems become trivial. All the fun is in expanding the boundaries of what is possible.
Tone Characteristics
Our writing should feel:
Conversational
Be serious and smart in a casual way. Write as if you're an optimistic, excited person sharing ideas you genuinely care about. Avoid corporate-speak and jargon that creates distance.
Thoughtful
Ground your writing in thoughtful analysis. If we're betting our future on understanding the market better than our competitors, then everything we write should demonstrate genuine thought.
Clear and Concise
Smart doesn't mean wordy. Use fewer words when possible. Have a good vocabulary, but keep things simple to help others understand our vision. Read your writing and clarify anything someone might not understand on the first pass.

data.title: Trial by Fire: The crash of Aeroflot flight 1492
data.author: shmeeed
data.article_summary: 2019年5月5日，俄罗斯国际航空（Aeroflot）1492航班在莫斯科谢列梅捷沃机场着陆后起火，导致机上41人遇难，37人幸存。这架苏霍伊超级喷气机100（Sukhoi Superjet 100）在着陆过程中遭遇雷暴和飞控系统故障，多次撞击跑道后起火。机尾迅速被火焰吞噬，部分乘客因毒烟丧生。事故引发了关于航空公司、飞机、机组人员及乘客责任的争议，尤其是一些乘客在撤离时仍试图拿取随身行李。经过近六年的调查，独立调查委员会发布了一份近600页的报告，指出事故原因复杂，包括天气、技术故障及人为因素。这起事故揭示了一个涉及广泛、技术复杂且带有悲剧性的故事。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：俄罗斯航空事故的原因分析及系统设计和安全文化问题

不同观点：
• **[mppm] 主要责任在于飞行员和航空公司**：
   - 80% 的责任归咎于飞行员错误，包括未严格遵循程序和清单，以及在紧急情况下的错误决策和操作。
   - 15% 的责任在于乘客取行李延误了撤离。
   - 5% 的责任归于飞机设计问题，但并不严重。
   - 认为紧急响应的延迟对结果影响不大，因为火势蔓延过快。

• **[andrewaylett] 系统设计和操作模式的转换问题**：
   - 质疑为何在紧急模式（Alternate and Direct Law）下操作与正常模式差别如此之大。
   - 建议紧急操作应尽量接近常规操作，以避免在紧急情况下增加操作复杂性。
   - 举例说明其他行业如何通过设计更安全的系统来应对紧急情况。

• **[the_mitsuhiko] 俄罗斯航空业的系统性问题**：
   - 认为事故是多个缺陷共同作用的结果，反映出俄罗斯整个航空行业的深层次问题。
   - 提到自2022年以来，俄罗斯航空事件在西方更难被评估，信息透明度下降。
   - 强调俄罗斯航空业存在制度性的冷漠文化，阻碍了安全改进。

• **[nativeit] 系统和机构的缺陷及对美国的警示**：
   - 强调事故揭示的系统和机构缺陷对美国也有警示作用。
   - 指出问责制、客观性、专业知识和透明度对安全的重要性。
   - 提及对俄罗斯事故的详细分析揭示了隐性问题的积累如何导致重大事故。

• **[rdtsc] 操作手册和数据错误问题**：
   - 提到SSJ操作手册中错误地包含了空客的控制法描述。
   - 指出SSJ机队中Direct Mode复现概率远高于预期，显示出制造商和运营方的数据问题。

Admiral Cloudberg

Aeroflot flight 1492 burns to the ground after landing at Moscow’s Sheremetyevo Airport. (ABC News Australia)
On the 5th of May 2019, travelers at Moscow’s biggest international airport were greeted by the astonishing sight of a passenger plane skidding down the runway in flames, its tail section engulfed by a conflagration of biblical proportions. As the crippled jet slid to a stop, the doors opened, the slides deployed, and passengers ran for their lives — but for many, the evacuation was over before it even began. In the back of the plane, the fire ripped into the cabin so quickly that some passengers perished without so much as a chance to stand up from their seats, while others collapsed in the aisle, enveloped in a cloud of toxic smoke from which they would never emerge. By the time the fire was out, half the plane stood intact, while half lay in ruins; and in a chilling mirror image of the vessel that carried them, 37 people walked away, while 41 others never came home.
The crash of a Russian-built Sukhoi Superjet 100, at a Russian airport, while flying for Russia’s flag carrier, set off a circular firing squad of accusations, as observers and stakeholders alike sought to determine whether fault lay with the airline, the airplane, the flight crew, or even the passengers, some of whom stopped to retrieve their carry-on bags while their countrymen burned. But the crash of Aeroflot flight 1492 isn’t a simple story. It ended in a wall of fire, but it began with a thunderstorm, a lightning strike, and a malfunction of the fly-by-wire control system, followed by a desperate return to the airport, an unstable descent and approach, and a botched landing attempt that slammed the plane into the runway over and over until it broke. The sequence of events was so long, raising so many complex questions, that it took investigators from the independent Interstate Aviation Committee nearly six years to reach firm conclusions and publish their report, which stretches to almost 600 pages and includes two dissenting opinions. The vast quantity of primary evidence, experimental data, and expert analysis contained in this new report finally permits a reasonably objective recounting of what actually happened on that blustery day in Moscow, in the process revealing a story that is colossal in breadth, mind-bendingly technical, and yet also at times frustratingly banal.
This is that story.
◊◊◊
A view over Sheremetyevo Airport. (Aviation Images Ltd.)
Part 1: Red Alarm
To be an airport firefighter requires acceptance of the principle that anticipation is more enjoyable than gratification. Yes, once in a while a fire erupts in a trash can or a piece of luggage, or someone spills some hydraulic fluid, but a great deal of time is spent either training for or standing ready for a career-defining catastrophe that most will never see. There is a certain frustration associated with the absence of a reason to put those skills to use, albeit one that is usually dispelled as soon as such a reason actually arises.
At Sheremetyevo International Airport, the world’s gateway to Moscow, the airport firefighting service is much like any other. Although Russia has a spotty aviation safety record, Sheremetyevo had long been spared, and by May of 2019 the greatest excitement within living memory for the airport firefighting service was a 2014 blaze aboard a mothballed Il-96. In an official statement, the airport declared that the soon-to-be-scrapped airliner was destroyed as a result of “spontaneous combustion.”
The 5th of May 2019 was a turbulent spring day, with thunderstorms bubbling up across the Moscow region. At Sheremetyevo Airport, the temperature by late afternoon had reached a pleasant 15˚C, with variable winds gusting up to 54 km/h amid intermittent light rain showers. Although Russia’s meteorological service had issued SIGMET thunderstorm warnings for the area, traffic at Sheremetyevo was no less heavy than usual. Throughout the afternoon, a flight took off every two minutes, climbing into the onrushing wind before turning sharply away toward clearer skies.
Unknown to the firefighters, one of those planes was coming back.
At 18:30 local time, a tremendous bang rang out over the airport, turning heads in the terminals and on the ramp toward Sheremetyevo’s runway 24 Left. And there they saw a plane, a little silver regional jet — or rather, just half of one, because the other half was lost somewhere in a firestorm of such tremendous size that witnesses could not believe it had only just now ignited, and yet it had. Flames and smoke billowing behind its wings and tail, the aircraft rolled down the runway at low speed with its nose gear extended but its belly dragging across the ground like a wounded dog. Within seconds, it began to slew to the left, its nose pivoting to face the terminal, whereupon it briefly appeared
43970363.article_summary: 2019年5月5日，俄罗斯国际航空（Aeroflot）1492航班在莫斯科谢列梅捷沃机场着陆后起火，导致机上41人遇难，37人幸存。这架苏霍伊超级喷气机100（Sukhoi Superjet 100）在着陆过程中遭遇雷暴和飞控系统故障，多次撞击跑道后起火。机尾迅速被火焰吞噬，部分乘客因毒烟丧生。事故引发了关于航空公司、飞机、机组人员及乘客责任的争议，尤其是一些乘客在撤离时仍试图拿取随身行李。经过近六年的调查，独立调查委员会发布了一份近600页的报告，指出事故原因复杂，包括天气、技术故障及人为因素。这起事故揭示了一个涉及广泛、技术复杂且带有悲剧性的故事。

data.title: Why are coffee stains darker at the edges?
data.author: michalpleban
data.article_summary: 当咖啡滴落并干燥后，污渍的边缘比中间颜色更深，这是因为液滴边缘的蒸发速度更快。尽管桌面看似光滑，实际上存在细微的不平整，使得液滴边缘受到阻碍，需要能量来缩小其周长。液滴上表面积大于下表面积，导致边缘蒸发更快，液体向边缘流动。随着液体蒸发，携带的咖啡颗粒也聚集在边缘，导致边缘的颜色更深。简而言之，更多携带咖啡颗粒的液体在边缘蒸发，使污渍边缘颜色更深。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：咖啡环效应的成因及相关现象

不同观点：
• **接触线钉扎效应的重要性**：croemer指出，接触线的钉扎效应（如由于表面粗糙度）是形成明显环状污渍的关键。如果是在光滑表面，液滴只会缩小，而不会形成环状污渍。
• **历史与应用**：nthingtohide提到，这种现象早在20年前的一个纪录片中就有解释，并提到该过程可用于制造极细的电线。
• **咖啡非均匀性**：Skunkleton质疑咖啡的非均匀性（如颗粒和油脂）是否也会影响环状污渍的形成，并提出毛细作用也是需要考虑的因素。
• **蒸发和毛细作用**：logic_node简单解释为液体蒸发时被拉到边缘，留下残留物形成环状。
• **水为何流向边缘**：nashashmi进一步提问为什么水会一直流向边缘，暗示对该现象的理解尚不完整。
• **多种因素共同作用**：kazinator详细解释了多种因素，包括毛细作用、蒸发速率和污渍面积的增加，导致污渍边缘颜色更深。
• **视觉错觉**：saltcured提到Mach带效应可能增强了环状污渍的对比度，使环状污渍看起来比实际更明显。

补充讨论：
• **其他类似现象**：vlan0提到不仅咖啡污渍，其他液体（如漏水导致的污渍）也有类似边缘变黑的现象。
• **工具与幽默**：rdtsc和ape4以幽默的方式提到LaTeX中的咖啡污渍包和网站域名的误解。
• **实际观察**：neogodless和thisismyswamp分享了个人观察和简要解释，支持蒸发和流体压力推动颗粒向外导致环状污渍的形成。

争议焦点：
• **咖啡环效应的主要成因**：Skunkleton和其他评论者对咖啡非均匀性和多种因素共同作用的讨论，表明对该现象的成因可能存在不同见解。
• **视觉错觉的影响**：saltcured提出的Mach带效应对环状污渍视觉增强的讨论，增加了对该现象理解的复杂性。

总体而言，讨论主要围绕咖啡环效应的物理成因及可能的视觉错觉展开，涉及蒸发、毛细作用、接触线钉扎和视觉感知等多方面因素。

Beint í
leiðarkerfi vefsins
.
Question
Why are coffee stains darkest at the edges when they dry?
Asked By
Gunnlaugur  Briem
Answer
There are many things around us that are so taken for granted that it never occurs to us to give them a second thought until we look a little closer. Coffee stains are one such thing. When coffee dries it leaves stains that are dark at the edges and lighter inside. The explanation may not be obvious but it is in fact rather simple.
When a drop lands on a table, it spreads and tries to dampen as large an area as possible. Though the table surface may seem smooth there are always some imperfections where the edges of the drop will stop. This can be compared to deep ruts in a track from which it is difficult to steer a vehicle's wheels.  In the same way the movement of the edges of the drop is hindered and it needs energy to diminish its circumference on the table.
Near the edge of the drop the upper surface slopes at an angle to the table surface. So the area of the drop's upper surface is greater than the area of its lower surface. Evaporation is in proportion to the drop's upper surface. So the evaporation per unit of area of the table surface is greatest at the edge of the drop.
The circumference and the edges of the drop remain unchanged as liquid in the drop evaporates. Because the evaporation is faster at the edges, liquid has to flow there. When all the liquid has evaporated, proportionately more has evaporated from the edges of the area that it covered on the table. There is a strong colour agent in coffee that is carried by the flow of liquid and remains when the liquid has evaporated. So the colour agent is in higher concentrations at the edges of the drop than in the middle. The same happens if we have a clear drop of water. As it has no colour agent we cannot see the process with our bare eyes.
It is best to understand this by looking at a cross-section of a coffee stain on a kitchen table. Image 1 shows a cross section of a new drop of coffee. Image 2 shows a cross-section of the same drop of coffee a little later, where it can be seen that it dries quickest at the edges. As it keeps the same shape, liquid is drawn to the edges of the drop and carries solid dark particles (coffee) with it. The final stage is shown in image 3 which is an exaggerated cross-section of the dark layer that remains when all the liquid has evaporated.
So the explanation in a nutshell is that more of the liquid carrying coffee particles, evaporates at the edges than in the centre. So more solids are deposited at the edges which means that the dark material is thicker there and darker than other parts of the stain.

• **工具与幽默**：rdtsc和ape4以幽默的方式提到LaTeX中的咖啡污渍包和网站域名的误解。
• **实际观察**：neogodless和thisismyswamp分享了个人观察和简要解释，支持蒸发和流体压力推动颗粒向外导致环状污渍的形成。

争议焦点：
• **咖啡环效应的主要成因**：Skunkleton和其他评论者对咖啡非均匀性和多种因素共同作用的讨论，表明对该现象的成因可能存在不同见解。
• **视觉错觉的影响**：saltcured提出的Mach带效应对环状污渍视觉增强的讨论，增加了对该现象理解的复杂性。

总体而言，讨论主要围绕咖啡环效应的物理成因及可能的视觉错觉展开，涉及蒸发、毛细作用、接触线钉扎和视觉感知等多方面因素。

data.title: Nextcloud cries foul over Google Play Store app rejection
data.author: brodo
data.article_summary: Nextcloud指责谷歌通过Play Store限制其Android文件同步应用的权限，特别是“所有文件访问”权限，导致该应用功能受限。Nextcloud称其应用自2016年起一直拥有该权限，但在2024年被无故撤销，而使用谷歌推荐的替代工具（如SAF或MediaStore API）无法满足需求。Nextcloud认为这是谷歌打击竞争的手段，并批评谷歌的申诉流程缓慢且无效。尽管Nextcloud在F-Droid上提供完整功能的版本，但Play Store版本受限影响了80多万用户。Nextcloud还提到曾向欧盟投诉微软等大公司的反竞争行为，但未见成效。谷歌未对此做出回应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Play Store的应用权限和安全政策及其影响

不同观点：
• pjc50、monegator等用户认为Google的权限限制过于严格，特别是在用户希望应用（如文件管理器或同步工具）能够访问所有文件的情况下。monegator分享了自己的经历，指出Google对应用相似性的规则执行不一致，导致开发者面临不必要的困难。
• mritzmann解释了背景，指出Google曾经允许某些权限，但现在变得更加严格，导致UX上的回归问题。
• SpaghettiCthulu和izacus认为Google的存储访问权限（如scoped storage）是合理的，用户应该能够控制应用访问哪些文件，而不是给予全盘访问权限。
• 0x000xca0xfe和conartist6从更广泛的角度讨论了软件限制和竞争环境，认为Google在安全和竞争之间需要找到平衡。

补充讨论：
• nopelynopington和rkagerer分享了个人使用Nextcloud的负面体验和Syncthing因政策问题放弃Android应用开发的情况。
• _def提到Dropbox的抽象层设计，认为某些应用为了与其他应用的集成不得不做出妥协。

• Google Play Store的权限政策是否过于严格，是否在安全和用户需求之间取得平衡。

43970959.article_content:
Applications
7
Nextcloud cries foul over Google Play Store app rejection
7
Claims policy change is really just a way to squeeze out competition
Richard Speed
Tue 13 May 2025
//
08:30 UTC
Exclusive
European software vendor Nextcloud has accused Google of deliberately crippling its Android Files application, which it says has more than 800,000 users.
The problem lies with the "
All files access
" permission, where broad access to files on a device is required. While most applications can make do with Google's more privacy-friendly storage access tools, such as Storage Access Framework (SAF) or the MediaStore API, others require more permissions – hence the "All files access" privilege.
Nextcloud's Android Files app is a file synchronization tool that, according to the company, has long had permission to read and write all file types. "Nextcloud has had this feature since its inception in 2016," it said, "and we never heard about any security concerns from Google about it."
That changed in 2024, when someone or something at Google's Play Store decided to revoke the permission, effectively crippling the application. Nextcloud was instructed to use "a more privacy-aware replacement."
According to Nextcloud, "SAF cannot be used, as it is for sharing/exposing our files to other apps ... MediaStore API cannot be used as it does not allow access to other files, but only media files."
Attempts to raise the issue with Google resulted in little more than copy-and-pasted sections of the developer guide. "Despite multiple appeals from our side and sharing additional background, Google is not considering reinstating upload for all files," Nextcloud said.
The issue seems to stem from the Play Store. While a fully functional version is available on F-Droid, the Play Store edition is subject to Google's imposed limitations. Regarding the All files access permission, Google's developer documentation
states
: "If you target Android 11 and declare All files access, it can affect your ability to publish and update your app on Google Play."
Nextcloud is clearly aggrieved by the change,
as are its users
.
"This might look like a small technical detail but it is clearly part of a pattern of actions to fight the competition," it said. "What we are experiencing is a piece of the script from the big tech playbook."
Microsoft gets twitchy over talk of Europe's tech independence
European biz calls for Euro tech for local people
Europe's cloud customers eyeing exit from US hyperscalers
Nextcloud puts out fire after data leak panic
Nextcloud cites examples, such as
allegations
leveled at Microsoft over the once-popular WordPerfect word processor, which were eventually
snuffed out
in 2014, or the antics of Apple and Meta that have
attracted scrutiny
from regulators.
In 2021, Nextcloud and other companies
filed a complaint
in the EU regarding alleged anti-competitive behavior from Microsoft. "We are now four years in, and nothing has happened," the company said. "What do you think happens to a company that releases no updates to their app in four years?"
Are there nefarious actors at play here, an automated process that auto-rejects apps with elevated access requirements, or is it just simple incompetence? "Either way," Nextcloud said, "it results in companies like ours just giving up, reducing functionality just to avoid getting kicked out of their app store."
"The issue is that small companies – like ours – have pretty much no recourse," it added. Nextcloud went on to criticize oversight processes as slow-moving, with fines that sound hefty but amount to little more than a slap on the wrist.
"Big Tech is scared that small players like Nextcloud will disrupt them, like they once disrupted other companies. So they try to shut the door."
Nextcloud told us the app's installed audience is 824,000 on Android - customers that used the app in the last 30 days.
The Register
repeatedly asked Google to comment, but it failed to respond. ®

data.title: We can no longer run Microsoft Store on 1809/LTSC 2019
data.author: fernvenue
data.article_summary: 该项目提供了一个适用于Windows LTSC版本的Microsoft Store软件包，支持Windows 10 LTSC 2019、2021以及Windows 11 LTSC 2024。由于LTSC 2019不再支持新版Microsoft Store，用户会被要求更新系统，且无法正常安装应用，因此该版本上的Microsoft Store已不可用，建议使用`Uninstall.bat`卸载。安装包可通过双击直接安装，但为确保兼容性，未使用最新版本的软件包，用户可能需要手动更新Microsoft Store。项目基于BSD-3-Clause许可证，包含安装和卸载脚本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“Microsoft Store”存储库出现在GitHub个人账户上的疑惑，以及对LTSC版本支持问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• bradford认为该GitHub存储库令人困惑，因为它是“Microsoft Store”相关的仓库，却在一个看似随机的个人账户上托管，且README文件没有清楚地解释该仓库的用途。他质疑提交者的意图，并提到LTSC版本缺乏支持并不是最令人困惑的部分。

• throitallaway支持bradford的观点，表示微软通过这种方式推广应用程序让人困惑。他分享了自己在Windows Server上安装Windows Terminal时遇到的困难，最终在GitHub发布页才找到所需内容。

• bongodongobob指出，如果用户使用的是LTSC版本，就不应该期望使用应用商店，因为LTSC版本是为那些有特定需求的关键应用程序而设，而不是为了应用商店。

• lousken关注winget（Windows软件包管理器）是否也会因此停止工作，暗示对微软应用分发机制的担忧。

• Havoc表达了对MS Store的不满，认为如果不再见到MS Store会是件好事，基于其负面的使用体验。

补充讨论：
• thangngoc89和steelbrain提供了背景信息，解释1809/LTSC 2019指的是Windows 10的长期支持版本，并说明LTSC在Windows术语中代表长期服务通道。

• doublerabbit和CamperBob2对该情况持轻松态度，认为这可能反而是件好事。

• Demiurge提出了一种假设性观点，认为如果Windows是开源的，这种情况可能可以避免，暗示开源可能带来更高的透明度和灵活性。

争议焦点：微软在LTSC版本上不提供MS Store支持的决定是否合理，以及通过GitHub分发关键应用程序的策略是否合适。用户对微软应用商店的体验和态度也存在分歧。

data.title: Launch HN: Miyagi (YC W25) turns YouTube videos into online, interactive courses
data.author: bestwillcui
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube学习工具的应用和优化

不同观点：
• clamlady：认为该工具可以扩展到YouTube上的语言学习内容，并对生物学相关内容受到关注感到高兴。同时对工具的实用性表示赞赏。
• EcommerceFlow：提出界面优化建议，包括讲座列表的整理和底部区域的简化，建议将多个功能整合到单个AI导师中，以提高用户体验。
• eochaid：对概念表示赞赏，但指出练习形式（填空而非选择题）可能不够友好，并提到AI导师互动较为平淡，闪卡部分效果不佳。
• jmathai：认为工具可以帮助发现广泛的主题内容，并提出利用chatgpt生成音频内容的学习方法。
• breakpointalpha：建议与德州扑克教学YouTube频道合作，以扩展内容种类。
• lassenordahl：对工具的概念表示赞赏，认为非常酷。
• vm：提到Bloom's 2-sigma研究，指出1对1辅导的巨大影响，并询问该研究在现代是否仍然有效。
• kubasienki：关注内容创作者的收入分享问题，质疑是否在未经许可的情况下使用内容。
• andrethegiant：关心在YouTube视频没有字幕的情况下工具是否能正常工作。
• skeeter2020：从edtech从业者的角度分析工具的挑战，指出工具执行效果不佳，并认为测验功能对目标市场价值有限，建议专注于上下文生成。
• sam1234apter：简单祝贺工具发布。
• pxndxx：关注内容创作者是否同意其内容被用于此工具。
• ix101：询问该工具是否适合用于二语学习。
• joshdavham：关心平台风险问题。
• bananapub：质疑如何验证生成内容的质量，以避免教授错误信息。

补充讨论：
• 工具的界面和功能整合是主要讨论点，EcommerceFlow和skeeter2020都提出了优化建议。
• 练习和测验形式的有效性存在争议，eochaid认为填空题不如选择题友好，skeeter2020则认为测验功能对目标市场价值有限。
• 内容创作者的权益问题被多次提及，kubasienki和pxndxx关注收入分享和内容许可问题。
• 工具的应用场景和内容质量验证也是讨论的重点，vm引用了学术研究来支持1对1辅导的有效性，bananapub则担心生成内容的准确性。

data.title: I learned Snobol and then wrote a toy Forth
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者学习Snobol语言的经历以及用Snobol编写的一个小型Forth解释器的项目。作者认为Snobol以其独特的模式匹配功能而令人着迷，尽管其控制流依赖于GOTO语句，属于1960年代的“非结构化编程”风格，通常认为在大型程序中会变得混乱。作者通过实现一个能运行“99 Bottles of Beer”程序的小型Forth解释器来验证自己对Snobol的理解，该解释器代码不到500行。作者建议在测试小型编程语言时设定一个目标程序，并分享了使用MNT Pocket Reform电脑和Krita软件完成项目的细节。

43951885.article_content:
This page is a mini-site for my Snobol excursion
with links to separate pages for my:
Thoughts on Snobol
Toy Forth interpreter written in Snobol
Thoughts about writing a toy Forth interpreter in Snobol
On with the show…​
I finally learned SNOBOL!
Snobol has been on my programming language bucket list for ages.
Snobol
Here’s my conclusions about the Snobol4 language itself, which get their own
pages:
Ratfactor’s Judgement of Snobol4
The Snobol Implementation Language (SIL)
In short, I think Snobol is fascinating. The singular focus on pattern matching
kind of reminds me of Awk. Except Awk doesn’t do nearly as much with patterns,
it devolves into a C-like script to do things with pattern matches.  Snobol
uses no such crutches, just pattern matching statements for all logic and
control flow.  Its purity is impressive.
No kidding:
Every single line
in a Snobol program consists of five parts:
label, subject, pattern, replacement, goto. All of those parts are optional.
That certainly makes it a Weird Language to the modern developer, but once you
get the hang of it, it’s easy to see why Snobol was once popular and
well-regarded by computer users of all stripes.
It’s extremely easy for seasoned developers to forget that even a simple loop
construct is a conceptual leap for beginners. I remember being that beginner.
By contrast, I think conditional GOTO-style control flow is easy for beginners
to follow because you can "see" it. You can trace the logic with your finger.
Of course, simplicity of language is good for programming in the small, but
maybe not so good for programming in the large.  Snobol4 is basically
1960s-style "unstructured programming", which is generally understood to
rapidly break down in large programs.
That’s the message in Edsger Dijkstra’s famous "Go To
Statement Considered Harmful" letter.
See David R. Tribble’s
Go To Statement Considered Harmful: A Retrospective
(david.tribble.com).
Still, Snobol proves that programming using "this one weird trick" can be surprisingly effective.
Snobol4th - A Forth in Snobol4
I’ve learned that it’s easy to think I understand a concept only to find
that I really don’t when forced to put it into practice. So I needed to make
some small project with Snobol to ensure I wasn’t fooling myself.
What to make?
"I know!" says Dave. "This is an opportunity to keep the concepts of the Forth
language fresh in my mind. I shall implement a toy Forth interpreter in
Snobol."
But
how much
Forth should I implement? Rather than go blindfolded and pick
language features at random, I decided to select a small Forth program to
execute. The goal would be: Once my implementation could execute it, I would be
done.
The program I picked is
99.forth
"99 Bottles of Beer"
by Arf Dysg and posted to one of my favorite programming-related websites:
http://www.99-bottles-of-beer.net/language-forth-793.html
And here’s the result, a Forth, written in Snobol, that executes a program that can run the above program that prints the complete lyrics of the "99 Bottles of Beer" song:
forth.sno
.
And here’s the result:
The Snobol4th Repo
The resulting Forth implementation is less than 500 lines of Snobol.
The README in the repo explains the program in greater detail and the
source of the interpreter is pretty readable - although it would be
a weird way to learn how Forth normally works.
Making toys to make toys
I really like this method of having a small target program.
A Forth interpreter put my Snobol knowledge to the test.
Forth is not my creation, but this strange implementation of Snobol4th
certainly is - both in its unusual execution and in the small subset of the
language I chose to implement. So for certain values of "my", I’ll call
this my toy programming language.
If you’re going to test out a small toy programming language of your own, I
think a target program is something to consider. Here’s a "card" I wrote about
this:
Have a target for your toy language
Speaking of cards, here’s the first one I wrote about Snobol before I dove all
the way in. For the modern developer, getting started with Snobol4 can be a bit
baffling. Here’s another small "card" page:
Getting started with Snobol
Colophon
I did this project late at night in bed when the rest of the family was asleep.
The computer pictured above is an
MNT Pocket Reform
.
I drew the little rat and snowball at the  top of this page with my favorite
FOSS drawing program,
Krita
.

data.title: In a high-stress work environment, prioritize relationships
data.author: wqtz
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在高压力工作环境中，优先考虑人际关系的重要性。在这种环境下，压力可能大到让人想辞职并对同事发怒。然而，作者提醒读者，每个人都在承受压力，你不是特例。即便工作看似可替代，但人际关系和印象却长久留存，未来的推荐信和职业机会仍依赖这些联系。因此，不要对人发火或撕破脸。在处理工作时，应关注如何影响他人，而不仅是截止日期或任务本身。保持人际关系的健康比单纯完成工作更重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工作环境中的人际关系与压力管理

不同观点：
• alphazard 认为，软件行业中，压力主要来源于不称职的同事，他们带来混乱和不确定性。与这类人保持礼貌距离是避免压力重复互动的关键，而与有能力且高效的同事相处则能带来积极体验。
• cj 提出，即使之前的工作经历很糟糕，在求职时仍应将其描绘得积极一些，以避免面试官对你的不满产生疑虑。
• jimkleiber 引用了名言，强调对每个人保持友善的重要性，因为每个人都在面对自己未知的战斗。这种心态有助于管理生活中的压力。
• neilv 指出，在高压力工作环境中，建立良好的人际关系不仅有助于未来推荐，还能在当下缓解环境带来的压力。但也要注意，过于依赖支持性关系可能会让人不愿离开有害的工作环境。
• itchyjunk 则表示，减少对人际关系的关注能减轻压力，专注于自己的事情更好，尽管这种方法因人而异。

补充讨论：
• dpe82 提到谷歌的一项研究，表明心理安全是团队高效工作的关键因素，强调了工作环境中安全感的重要性。
• _ink_ 和 BartSpaans 强调了同理心和人际关系在职场中的重要性，认为社交能力往往比工作能力本身更重要。
• zphds 和 ArthurStacks 提醒大家在高压环境下保持健康生活方式的重要性，特别是良好的睡眠和饮食。
• taraindara 和 Daisywh 分享了个人经历，强调在困难时期意识到自己并不孤单是一种安慰，良好的人际关系有时能在关键时刻提供帮助。

争议焦点：
• 关于是否应在高压力环境中投入精力建立人际关系存在不同看法。neilv 认为支持性关系能缓解压力，但也会让人不愿离开有害环境；而 itchyjunk 则认为减少对人际关系的关注能更有效减轻压力。
• 另一个争议点是关于如何在求职时描述过去的工作经历，cj 建议将其美化以避免负面印象，而 junikaefer 则表示在某些地区，背景调查并不重要。

总的来说，讨论围绕如何在高压力工作环境中处理人际关系和管理压力展开，不同观点强调了个人经验和策略的多样性。

43972535.article_content:
In a high-stress work environment, prioritize relationships
13 May, 2025
How high is the stress I am talking about? You are commuting all you think is that you might snap today, you might quit today. That is what I am calling a high-stress work environment. You know after a certain point the job becomes disposable and you are making a list in your head of who you are going to say "fuck you" to as you storm out of the building.
The reality in this environment is that everyone is stressed and you are not unique. The person pressing you is being pressed on by another guy. Everyone hates their job and everyone likes the movie "Office Space" daydreaming about quitting and dating Jennifer Aniston, who happens to be beautiful but stupid enough to not see that.
The reality is that if you quit, you DO NEED these connections to get a new job in the form of a recommendation. Do not snap at people. You may think the job is disposable, but the reality is that the memory is not. You will always be "that guy". You will always be the person who said "fuck you" to them, even though you were both in a pile of shit neck-deep.
So, prioritize relationships. If you are doing something, forget about deadlines or significance, think of the other person who is begging you and how it impacts them. Every relationship is a human relationship, so do not let the "professional environment" corrupt that.

data.title: Show HN: A5
data.author: pheelicks
data.article_summary: A5是一个开源的全球等面积地理空间索引系统，基于五边形对十二面体进行划分，提供32种不同分辨率级别，最小单元面积小于30平方毫米。A5的单元格具有统一的面积（误差在2%以内），适用于表示城市区域或土地等空间数据，便于进行空间分析和聚合点数据。与其它DGGS（离散全球网格系统）相比，A5具有均匀的单元大小、高分辨率（64位整数编码）、以及最小化的全球单元区域畸变。A5使用TypeScript实现，遵循Apache 2.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同空间索引系统（A5, H3, S2, HEALPix等）的优缺点及适用场景

不同观点：
• **[knowitnone]** 建议在标题中添加描述，以便更直观地理解何时使用该系统。

• **[carderne]** 提出A5相比H3的优势：
  - A5分辨率更高，比H3高约4个数量级。
  - A5的单元格大小更一致（平方米上相等），而H3的单元格大小可能相差约2倍。
  同时，提出A5的缺点：形状不规则，中心点间距离不一致。

• **[xioxox]** 询问A5与HEALPix相比的优势，HEALPix也是一种常用的地理空间索引方法。

• **[Tabular-Iceberg]** 分享了自己曾经无意中创建了一个DGG（离散全球网格），但项目未继续，不确定是否可行，暗示A5可能在某些方面不如其他实现。

• **[yencabulator]** 比较了多个系统：
  - Google的S2注重性能和前缀匹配。
  - Uber的H3通过复杂数学计算，减少中心点间距离的变化，适用于驾驶时间优化。
  - A5进一步复杂化数学计算，减少远距离单元格面积变化，适用于分析密度等场景。

• **[pheelicks]** 提供了一个可视化解释和互动示例的链接，帮助理解A5的工作原理。

• **[jll29]** 指出A5使用五边形，而H3使用六边形，并提供了H3的参考链接。

• **[Bedon292]** 询问A5是否仅适用于数据可视化，还是在数据库搜索等场景中也能带来性能提升。

• **[zX41ZdbW]** 提到H3和S2在ClickHouse中开箱即用，并有C和C++库，但A5仅有TypeScript实现，虽然移植不难。

• **[ralusek]** 质疑优化最低顶点曲率（A5基于十二面体）的必要性，认为一般场景下S2或H3已经足够，想不出为何要选择A5。

补充讨论：
- A5的分辨率和单元格一致性被认为是其主要优势，但其不规则形状和复杂的数学计算可能限制其应用场景。
- 讨论中涉及多个空间索引系统的比较，包括S2、H3、HEALPix和A5，每个系统在特定应用中都有其独特的优势和局限性。

A5
- Global, equal-area, millimeter-accurate geospatial index
Website:
A5Geo.org
Introduction
A5 is a geospatial index that partitions the world into
pentagonal cells
. The cells are available at
32 different resolution levels
, with the largest cell covering the whole world, and the smallest less than 30mm². Within each resolution level the cells have equal area, to
within 2%
.
A5 cells provide simple way to represent spatial data as a collection of cells, which together represent regions on the globe. These can be anything, from city districts to parcels of land. Once data is in a cell-based format, it becomes much simpler to perform analysis such as calculating the correlation between different variables - for example elevation and crop yield.
Cells can also be used to group (aggregate) point data, to understand how it spatially distributed. For example, the
density of holiday rentals
across a city.
To understand how it works, take a look at the
Examples
.
A5 is implemented in TypeScript and is available as a
library
, with
API documentation here
. It is
open source
and licensed under the
Apache 2.0 License
.
Benefits over alternative systems
Like other
DGGSs
, A5 can be used for indexing, spatial joins, and other spatial operations. The appropriate choice of DGGS will depend on the use case, the key strengths of A5 over other similar indexing systems are:
Uniform cell sizes group spatial features without introducing bias due to unequal cell sizes.
Very high resolution of 30mm² at final resolution level, encoded as a 64-bit integer.
Minimal distortion of cell areas across the globe.
Geometric Construction
DGGSs
are generally based on a planar cell tiling which is applied to the sides of a
platonic solid
, before being projected onto a sphere.
A5 is unique in that it uses a pentagonal tiling of a dodecahedron. The
pentagon chosen
for the tiling is equilateral, but not regular - unlike other common DGGSs which use regular polygons, for example
HTM
uses triangles,
S2
uses squares, and
H3
uses hexagons.
The benefit of choosing a dodecahedron is that it is the platonic solid with the lowest vertex curvature, and by this measure it is the most spherical of all the platonic solids. This is key for minimizing cell distortion as the process of projecting a platonic solid onto a sphere involves warping the cell geometry to force the vertex curvature to approach zero. Thus, the lower the original vertex curvature, the less distortion will be introduced by the projection.

data.article_summary: 欧洲漏洞数据库（EUVD）已全面运行，提供一个简化的平台来监控关键和正在被利用的安全漏洞。在美国因预算削减和披露延迟导致其自身漏洞跟踪系统陷入困境之际，欧盟推出EUVD，旨在提高漏洞管理效率和透明度。与美国的国家漏洞数据库（NVD）类似，EUVD标识每个披露的漏洞，注明其严重性和利用状态，并提供可用的补救措施和补丁链接。不同的是，EUVD几乎实时更新，并突出显示关键和被利用的漏洞。EUVD提供三个仪表板视图，信息来源于开源数据库、各国CSIRT的建议和警报，以及供应商发布的补救和修补指南。ENISA作为CVE编号机构，也在与MITRE沟通，以了解美国CVE计划的未来影响。
