E-COM: The $40 million USPS project to send email on paper
The USPS offered to print your email for you. Only spammers said yes.
Email, for just under three years, came in a blue-and-white envelope from the United States Postal Service.
Every new technology, it seemed—telegrams, telephones, faxes, and faster delivery services alike—had threatened the Postal Service’s monopoly on delivering the mail.
This time, the threat seemed existential. A 1982
Congressional report predicted
that “Two-thirds or more of the mailstream could be handled electronically,” and “the volume of mail is likely to peak in the next 10 years.”
Good thing the mailmen were ready. The Post Office had landed on a plan to co-opt the email revolution.
How do you get email to the folks without computers? What if the Post Office printed out email, stamped it, dropped it in folks’ mailboxes along with the rest of their mail, and saved the USPS once and for all?
And so in 1982 E-COM was born—and, inadvertently, helped coin the term “e-mail.”
Mail on the wire
The original study that recommended the USPS start sending email, for everyone.
It all started in 1971, when the Post Office Department was rebranded for the first time in its 179-year history and turned into the United States Postal Service. Through snow, rain, sleet, and gloom, they got nearly 87 billion pieces of mail through that year.
It’d weathered the elements, and now it needed to weather sweeping technological changes. So among the newly christened USPS’s first acts was to open an Advanced Service department and hire ex-Peace Corps analyst Gene Johnson to run it and decide how mail of the future should look.
The Postal Service had long adapted by embracing the new. Jeeps in lieu of horses, Zone Improvement Plan (or ZIP, as we’d come to know them) codes to automate mail sorting. The USPS couldn’t beat telegrams for speed, so they embraced them with a Western Union partnership to send
“Mailgrams” next-day through the mail for $2.75
(a moderate success, that—incredibly—
ran until Western Union terminated telegram service in 2006
).
The next frontier to conquer: Electronic mail.
“There was billions of billions of billions of pieces [of mail] that were computer-generated,” said Johnson to Devin Leonard in his book “
Neither Snow nor Rain: A History of the United States Postal Service
.” That gave Johnson an idea. Each of those letters that were currently being created on computers, printed, and mailed, could instead “be sent directly from the computer into the Postal Service and sent out to the post offices for printing and delivering,” he surmised.
This could be big. Fifty million letters a year big, according to the Postal Service’s projections.
A diagram of the USPS’ ideas for how to deliver email—in print, and eventually online
So they went to the drawing board, and designed email on paper. The
pitch was simple
: “We convert your message, up to 2 pages, into hard copy. We fold it and insert it into an envelope. We seal the envelope and put it into the mailstream. Then, we deliver your message anywhere in the continental U.S.”
E-COM messages could be one or two pages long, with
up to 41 lines of text on the first page
and 56 lines on the second. You’d type up the messages, then send them via TTY or IBM 2780/3789 terminals to one of 25 post offices. There, a Sperry Rand Univac 1108 computer system would receive your messages.
E-COMs could be “Single Address Messages” with a letter for a single recipient, “Common Text Messages” with a single bulk letter intended for multiple recipients, or “Text Insertion Messages” with form letters blended with text to be inserted into the message for an early take on
mail merge
. The Univac would print your emails, then postal staff would fold them, stuff them in envelopes, and send them on their way.
The team had this one shot to keep the Post Office afloat. “In the future, the only way the Postal Service will be able to keep its volume rising and finances dependable is through participating in electronic mail services,” read the
1979 Annual Report of the Postmaster General
.
And then bureaucracy bit.
Email by fiat
The first print use of the word “e-mail” as the FCC worked to stop the Postal Service from sending electronic messages
Optimism prevailed at first. Postmaster General William Bolger suggested charging the price of a stamp—15¢, at the time—per E-COM message, and even thought they could lower the price over time. The team promised two-day delivery, but that too they hoped to reduce to one day with volume.
And, perhaps, that volume would be easier to hit, imagined the Post Office, if Congress would authorize an expanded monopoly. The Postal Service proposed it should have “monopoly over delivery of hard copy associated with electronic messages,”
said Postal Rate Commission chairman Janet Steiger

data.title: Databricks and Neon
data.author: davidgomes
data.article_summary: Databricks宣布收购Neon，一家以开发者优先的无服务器Postgres公司。Neon团队开发了一种新的数据库架构，提供高速、弹性扩展以及分支和分叉功能，非常适合开发者和AI代理使用。Neon实现了存储和计算的分离，使开发者可以在几秒钟内创建Postgres实例，并自动根据负载调整扩展，简化了数据库操作。此外，Neon支持数据库的即时分支和分叉，方便实验和测试。有趣的是，Neon数据库有超过80%由AI代理创建，得益于其快速部署、弹性扩展和低成本优势。Neon的创始人与Databricks在技术创新和开源理念上有着共同的DNA，这将有助于为AI时代提供强大的无服务器数据库基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Neon 被 Databricks 收购的影响及相关技术选择

不同观点：
• **支持Neon团队，但对收购持谨慎态度**：
   - 恭喜Neon团队（beoberha, jlengrand），但担心VC资金导致的不可避免的收购（beoberha）。
   - 希望Neon在Databricks下仍能保持独立性和用户关注（higeorge13, timmg）。
   - 担心Databricks会改变Neon的核心价值或使其变得昂贵（flanked-evergl, acd10j）。

• **对Databricks的批评和质疑**：
   - 认为Databricks定价高且核心业务正在商品化（jamesblonde）。
   - Databricks被比作Oracle，暗示其可能 ruin Neon 或使其变得昂贵（flanked-evergl, acd10j）。
   - Databricks被批评为难以使用且令人沮丧（flanked-evergl）。

• **对Neon技术及替代方案的讨论**：
   - 讨论Neon作为PostgreSQL的替代方案，特别是其解决操作问题的潜力（kjuulh）。
   - 对Neon技术栈和其相对于其他选项（如AWS RDS, Aurora, CockroachDB, Yugabyte）的优势和不足进行比较（kjuulh）。
   - 有人询问Neon的替代方案，并讨论了自托管PostgreSQL的挑战和维护负担（kjuulh, Squarex）。

• **对Neon开源和商业模式的疑问**：
   - 有人质疑Neon的开源性质和商业模式，询问为何用户要付费而不是自托管（amazingamazing）。

补充讨论：
• **Neon团队的回应**：
   - Neon工程师提供了有关收购的常见问题解答链接，以回应社区的关注（davidgomes）。

• **相关链接**：
   - 提供了Neon的博客文章和WSJ文章链接，供进一步阅读（lmc）。

• **市场趋势和估值讨论**：
   - 提到当前市场对“无服务器”和“AI相关”技术的估值高涨，并预测未来12个月将有大量现金收购（dan_goosewin）。

争议的焦点：
• Databricks收购Neon后是否会保持Neon的独立性和用户友好性，还是会因企业策略而损害Neon的核心价值。

Summary
We’re excited to announce that we have agreed to acquire
Neon
, a developer-first serverless Postgres company
The Neon team engineered a new database architecture that offers speed, elastic scaling, and branching and forking. The capabilities that make Neon great for developers are also great for AI agents
Together, we'll deliver an open, serverless database foundation for developers and AI agents
Today, we are excited to announce that we have agreed to acquire
Neon
, a developer-first, serverless Postgres company. Neon’s co-founders are among the very few people in the world who could re-architect Postgres with true separation of storage and compute, built for modern developers and AI systems. Their world-class team of Postgres hackers and database veterans will join Databricks to deliver serverless Postgres at production scale to developers in an AI-native world.
A developer-first mission, born from Postgres expertise
Four years ago, the Neon co-founders joined together with a vision to disrupt the database industry. They observed that the foundations of database technologies were largely designed for the 90s era. Their goal was to build a new database platform that would dramatically improve experiences for developers, in some fundamental ways:
They foresaw that Postgres would become the de facto standard for databases and had the vision to create a serverless Postgres platform.
They were determined to make it possible to create a new Postgres instance in seconds, so developers wouldn’t need to wait.
They set out to simplify the operational aspect of database scaling by automating it as load changed, so developers could start very small and not worry about over- or under-provisioning.
They wanted to enable rapid experimentation and testing by supporting instant forking and branching of databases and creating fully isolated databases, as databases are often one of the most difficult modules to test in end-to-end application testing.
A few years in, the Neon team engineered a new, innovative database architecture that decouples storage scaling from compute scaling, which ultimately enabled all of the above goals. When Neon first launched, developers raved about the speed, the simplicity, and the ability to branch and fork their databases like Git does for code.
The shift toward AI agents
As Neon became GA last year, they noticed an interesting stat: 30% of the databases were created by AI agents, not humans. When they looked at their stats again recently, the number went from 30% to over 80%. That is,
AI agents were creating 4 times more databases versus humans
.
If you think of AI agents as your own massive team of high-speed junior developers (potentially “mentored” by senior developers), it’s then not surprising that the same capabilities the Neon team focused on that made Neon great for developers also made Neon great for these AI agents:
Postgres open source ecosystem
: All frontier LLMs have been trained on the vast amount of public information available about the Postgres open source ecosystem, so all AI agents are experts in using Neon, which is built on Postgres.
Speed
: Traditional databases were designed for humans to provision and operate. It was OK to take minutes to spin up a database. Given AI agents operate at machine speed, ultra rapid provisioning time becomes critical.
Elastic scaling and pricing:
The decoupled storage from compute serverless architecture enables extremely low-cost Postgres instances. It’s now possible to launch thousands or even millions of agents with their own databases cost-effectively.
Branching and forking
: AI agents can be non-deterministic, and “vibes” need to be checked and verified. Neon’s ability to instantly create a full copy of a database, not only for schema but also for the data, allows all these AI agents to be operating on their own isolated database instance in high fidelity for experimentation and validation.
Shared DNA
We have long known Nikita Shamgunov, Heikki Linnakangas, and Stas Kelvich – the founders of Neon. Before Neon, Nikita started his career working on SQL Server and later became well-known in the database community as a co-founder and CEO of SingleStore, driving the startup’s business to over $100M in annual revenue. Heikki has been a committer on Postgres for two decades - he started his Postgres journey when he was bored on paternity leave and decided to look into Postgres internals for fun. Stas is an ex-physicist who got into Postgres hacking because he needed a better R-tree implementation for his tourism search engine startup.
Databricks and Neon share the same DNA in building hardcore technical innovations at the infrastructure layer. We also share the belief in the importance of open source: we originally started the Apache Spark™ project at UC Berkeley, which also happens to be the original birthplace of Postgres, the open source database project Neon builds
43982777.article_summary: Databricks宣布收购Neon，一家以开发者优先的无服务器Postgres公司。Neon团队开发了一种新的数据库架构，提供高速、弹性扩展以及分支和分叉功能，非常适合开发者和AI代理使用。Neon实现了存储和计算的分离，使开发者可以在几秒钟内创建Postgres实例，并自动根据负载调整扩展，简化了数据库操作。此外，Neon支持数据库的即时分支和分叉，方便实验和测试。有趣的是，Neon数据库有超过80%由AI代理创建，得益于其快速部署、弹性扩展和低成本优势。Neon的创始人与Databricks在技术创新和开源理念上有着共同的DNA，这将有助于为AI时代提供强大的无服务器数据库基础。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕树木数据库及相关网站资源的讨论，涉及技术问题、情感反应及对古树保护的争议。

不同观点：
• **[pjc50]** 提供了存档链接，指出某些相关资源已经开始老化，并提供了两个有趣的示例链接，引导用户查看。
• **[ta1243]** 认为公众对Sycamore Gap树被砍倒的反应过于激烈，指出相比之下，一家连锁餐馆砍掉一棵500年老树时却没有类似的全国性讨论。质疑为何对不同事件的反应存在双重标准。
• **[JimDabell]** 对讨论进行了扩展，推荐了另一个相关资源OpenTrees.org，介绍了该网站作为市政树木数据库的价值。

补充讨论：
• **[whywhywhywhy]** 对OpenTrees.org网站的用户体验提出批评，指出地图标记消失、图片无法显示等问题，认为这使得浏览和寻找树木变得繁琐。
• **[hermitcrab]** 对OpenTrees.org使用"inventory"一词表示不满，认为古树不应仅仅被视作商业库存，而应有更高的文化和生态价值。
• **[Namari]** 提到网站存在加载问题，尤其是当指向默认城市以外的其他城市时，网站无法正常显示内容。
• **[metalman]** 提到最近3-4年在英格兰发生的一起事件，某棵具有文学关联的老树及其周围草地被毁，用于修建环岛，表达了对历史遗产保护不力的不满。

争议焦点：
• 公众对不同树木被毁事件的反应不一，尤其是[ta1243]提出的关于Sycamore Gap树和500年老树的对比，引发了对社会双重标准的质疑。
• 关于OpenTrees.org网站的用户体验和技术问题，[whywhywhywhy]等用户指出其地图功能存在缺陷，影响了实用性。
• 对古树的定义和保护态度存在分歧，[hermitcrab]认为不应将古树简单视作"inventory"，而应赋予更高的文化和生态意义。

data.title: $20K Bounty Offered for Optimizing Rust Code in Rav1d AV1 Decoder
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了rav1d AV1解码器的性能提升悬赏计划。rav1d是一个用Rust编写的安全高性能AV1解码器，目前其性能比C语言编写的dav1d解码器慢约5%。为了解决这一问题，开发团队提供20,000美元的奖金池，邀请个人或团队帮助提升rav1d的性能，使其达到dav1d的性能水平。参赛者需为美国、英国、欧盟、加拿大、新西兰或澳大利亚的合法居民或公民，且改进必须在Rust代码或Rust编译器、标准库中进行，不允许使用其他语言。参赛者需按照项目贡献流程提交改进，并通过指定方式参与悬赏。最终奖金将根据性能提升的比例分配，由开发团队酌情决定奖励对象。详情和规则可在官方页面查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust与C语言在性能优化中的比较、代码奖励的合理性以及特定优化竞赛的奖金和参与资格问题。

不同观点：
• **Rust和C语言性能对比**：
  - **pizza234**：在将代码从非安全移植到Rust的安全代码时，性能有所下降（约11%）。特别是在去除指针并使用Rust的安全类型后，边界检查和缓冲区初始化成为了问题。
  - **IshKebab**：对Rust的性能下降感到惊讶，认为5%的性能差异不应成为选择C语言而非Rust的理由，怀疑背后有其他非技术性原因。

• **奖金金额的合理性**：
  - **Ragnarork**：认为2万美元对于这种复杂和高要求的优化工作来说太低了，难以达到最先进水平（如dav1d）。
  - **feverzsj**：认为至少需要200万美元才能完成这种优化工作。
  - **bluGill**：指出2万美元只能支付最多一周的工作，对于专业人士来说不值得投入，除非他们本来就想免费做。长期来看，需要至少6个月的资助才合理。

• **代码奖励的道德性**：
  - **4ad**：认为代码奖励是不道德的，因为只有少数人能获得报酬，而参与者大多处于经济困境。这种模式利用了他们的困境。

• **竞赛参与资格**：
  - **degurechaff**：质疑为何亚洲人不能参与。
  - **minraws**：指出竞赛仅对特定国家开放，导致许多有能力的开发者无法参与。

补充讨论：
• **对优化竞赛的兴趣**：
  - **jebarker**：希望有人能发起类似于Kaggle的软件优化竞赛。
  - **dblohm7**：希望看到有人使用Halide构建生产解码器。
  - **bArray**：希望看到2万美元奖金用于优化dav1d解码器，以衡量投入和产出的关系。

• **技术实现的难度**：
  - **rvz**：强调这次优化任务必须准确无误，不能依赖聊天机器人如ChatGPT等完成。

• **奖励平台的推荐**：
  - **irf1**：推荐使用https://algora.io平台发布开源奖励和合同工作，并提供联系方式以获取更多信息。

争议焦点：
- **奖金金额是否合理**：专业人士认为2万美元不足以补偿所需的工作量和专业技能，而有些人则认为即使如此也应该吸引到参与者。
- **代码奖励的道德性**：一方认为奖励模式不公平且不道德，另一方则可能认为这是一种合理的市场行为。
- **竞赛参与的国籍限制**：许多开发者对竞赛仅限于特定国家表示不满。

43982238.article_content:
$20,000 rav1d AV1 Decoder Performance Bounty
In March of 2023 we
announced
that we were starting work on a safer high performance AV1 decoder called
rav1d
, written in Rust. We partnered with
Immunant
to do the engineering work. By September of 2024 rav1d was basically complete and we
learned a lot
during the process. Today rav1d works well—it passes all the same tests as the dav1d decoder it is based on, which is written in C. It’s possible to build and run Chromium with it.
There’s just one problem—it’s not quite as fast as the C version. We want to change that and we need your help.
Our Rust-based rav1d decoder is currently about 5% slower than the C-based dav1d decoder (the exact amount differs a bit depending on the benchmark, input, and platform). This is enough of a difference to be a problem for potential adopters, and, frankly, it just bothers us. The development team worked hard to get it to performance parity. We brought in a couple of other contractors who have experience with optimizing things like this. We
wrote about the optimization work we did
. However, we were still unable to get to performance parity and, to be frank again, we aren’t really sure what to do next.
After racking our brains for options, we decided to offer a bounty pool of $20,000 for getting rav1d to performance parity with dav1d. Hopefully folks out there can help get rav1d performance advanced to where it needs to be, and ideally we and the Rust community will also learn something about how Rust performance stacks up against C.
The
official rules are here
, but to summarize:
The contest is open to individuals or teams of individuals who are legal residents or citizens of the United States, United Kingdom, European Union, Canada, New Zealand, or Australia.
The rules provide instructions for benchmarking performance improvements.
You work on improving performance. Your improvements can be in rav1d, the Rust compiler, or the Rust standard library.
The dav1d and rav1d decoders share the exact same low-level assembly code optimizations—you cannot modify this assembly. You must improve the Rust code (or the Rust compiler), which is what differs between dav1d and rav1d. You may not introduce code into rav1d in a language other than Rust. We encourage you to ask questions early on in issues or by
emailing us
so as to avoid investing heavily in something that might not be eligible!
Get your performance improvements merged into the relevant project per the project's standard contribution process and under its open source license(s), then email us per the instructions in the
official rules
to enter and potentially be rewarded for your contribution.
When the contest ends (likely either because we met our goal or time has run out) we will, at our discretion, divide the bounty proportionally between the largest contributors to performance gains.
At the end of the day, we reserve the right to award the money to the person(s) or team(s) that we deem to have helped us reach or exceed performance parity in the best possible way.
If we update the rules we'll post a note here and on the official rules page.
Good luck! Have fun!

data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：城市设计与家庭、社会问题（如犯罪、无家可归者）之间的关联

不同观点：
• flanked-evergl认为城市设计并不是问题，真正的问题在于现代社会的反家庭倾向。他指出，社会不断向人们传递不生孩子或独自生活更好的观念，再加上犯罪问题和税收制度中对不承担责任者的补贴，都对家庭生活构成挑战。

• fullshark指出无家可归者问题是讨论中被忽视的重要议题，暗示在讨论城市设计时不能忽略这一群体的存在和需求。

• vanschelven的评论侧重于对文章本身的解读，指出文章宣布了一系列子文章获得了普利策奖，但没有深入讨论城市或家庭问题。

• brudgers通过提到 skate parks 的例子，指出小城市的公共设施（如滑板公园）是家庭友好设计的一部分，并提供了一个链接以供参考。

• peterhadlaw强调控制犯罪是城市生活的基础，认为如果无法和平共处，那么其他讨论都没有意义。

补充讨论：
• toomuchtodo 提供了一个存档链接，但没有进一步的评论或解释，可能意在为讨论提供背景资料或存档参考。

争议焦点：
• 不同评论者对城市问题的根源有不同看法。flanked-evergl认为反家庭的社会设计和观念是主要问题，而fullshark则强调无家可归者问题的紧迫性。peterhadlaw则认为犯罪问题是其他讨论的前提。

• 对城市设计的关注点不同，有人关注家庭友好设施（如brudgers提到的滑板公园），有人则关注更广泛的社会和犯罪问题（如flanked-evergl和peterhadlaw）。

data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 研究团队开发了一种高分辨率的远程成像系统，利用多束激光照射远距离目标，并通过两台望远镜收集反射光。该系统基于强度干涉测量技术，能够在一公里以上的距离成像毫米级的文字，分辨率较单台望远镜提升了14倍。与常见的振幅干涉测量不同，强度干涉测量通过比较两个探测器接收光强波动的相关性来获取空间信息。为了克服激光相干性带来的噪声问题，研究人员将100毫瓦的激光分成八束，每束光经过不同大气路径，获得不同的随机相位扰动，从而实现可观测的干涉效果。实验中，团队成功重建了1.36公里外目标上的字母图像。这项技术有望应用于大气湍流下的光学成像和生物医学成像等领域。

May  9, 2025

Physics
18, 99
A high-resolution imaging system captures distant objects by shining laser light on them and detecting the reflected light.
L.-C. Liu
et al.
[
1

Seeing the small picture.
The remote-imaging system (left) shoots eight infrared laser beams (red line added to show the path) at a target (right) in a building 1.36 km away. Light reflecting off the target is collected by the system’s two telescopes.
L.-C. Liu
et al.
[
1
]
Seeing the small picture.
The remote-imaging system (left) shoots eight infrared laser beams (red line added to show the path) at a target (right) in a building 1.36 km away. Light reflecting off the target is collected by the system’s two telescopes.
×
One of astronomers’ tricks for observing distant objects is intensity interferometry, which involves comparing the intensity fluctuations recorded at two separate telescopes. Researchers have now applied this technique to the imaging of remote objects on Earth [
1
]. They developed a system that uses multiple laser beams to illuminate a distant target and uses a pair of small telescopes to collect the reflected light. The team demonstrated that this intensity interferometer can image millimeter-wide letters at a distance of 1.36 km, a 14-fold improvement in spatial resolution compared with a single telescope.
Interferometry is common in radio astronomy, where the signal amplitudes from a large array of radio telescopes are summed together in a way that depends on the relative phases of the radio waves. Intensity interferometry is something else. It doesn’t involve addition of amplitudes or preservation of phases. Instead, light is recorded from a single source at two separate detectors (or telescopes), and the fluctuations in the intensities of the two signals are compared. Spatial information on the source comes from analyzing how these fluctuations are correlated in time and how this correlation depends on the detector separation.
The correlations can be hard to understand intuitively, and there are both quantum and classical explanations. One quantum description involves two-photon interference. Imagine that photon 1 comes from the left side of the source and arrives at detector A at the same time that photon 2 comes from the right side of the source and arrives at detector B. That scenario is observationally indistinguishable from photon 1 arriving at B and photon 2 arriving at A. The indistinguishability leads to quantum interference that causes a simultaneous fluctuation in intensity at the detectors. This correlation decreases as the separation between detectors is increased.
With a first demonstration in 1956, intensity interferometry has proven useful in measuring star diameters [
2
]. Still, the technique is less common than amplitude interferometry, as the latter typically offers a stronger signal compared to the noise. But there are “disordered” situations where the light is partially scrambled and amplitude interferometry becomes challenging, says Qiang Zhang from the University of Science and Technology of China. These situations include optical imaging in the presence of atmospheric turbulence and biomedical imaging through tissues.
L.-C. Liu
et al
. [
1
]
Far-sighting.
Left: The interferometer system includes multilasers for illuminating the target and a pair of detectors for collecting the reflected light. Right: Four letter targets are shown with their reconstructed images.
L.-C. Liu
et al
. [
1
]
Far-sighting.
Left: The interferometer system includes multilasers for illuminating the target and a pair of detectors for collecting the reflected light. Right: Four letter targets are shown with their reconstructed images.
×
Until now, intensity interferometry targets have been either bright distant objects (such as stars) or nonluminous objects that can be illuminated by a nearby source. Zhang and his colleagues have now developed an intensity interferometer for remote imaging through the atmosphere. It consists of two telescopes and an infrared laser system installed on the same optical bench. The laser light illuminates the target object, which in the team’s tests was located in another building 1.36 km away.
The main challenge is that laser light is coherent—the photons have related phases—which causes the observed intensity fluctuations to be dominated by the internal variations in the laser (so-called shot noise). To avoid this problem, the team divided their 100-milliwatt laser into eight beams. Each beam travels along a slightly different path through the turbulent atmosphere and thus receives a different random phase perturbation. Counterintuitively, this incoherent illumination makes the interference effects observable.

data.title: Show HN: acmsg (automated commit message generator)
data.author: qeden
data.article_summary: **acmsg** 是一个使用 OpenRouter API 的自动化 Git 提交消息生成工具，用 Python 编写。它可以分析 Git 仓库中的暂存更改，并通过 AI 生成上下文相关的提交消息。主要功能包括支持多种 AI 模型、可选编辑生成的消息，以及在确认后自动提交更改。安装可通过 pipx 或 Nix 包管理器进行，并需要 OpenRouter API 密钥。配置文件位于 `~/.config/acmsg/config.yaml`，初次运行时会提示设置 API 密钥。使用命令包括 `commit` 生成提交消息和 `config` 管理配置。该工具基于 MIT 许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在生成和改进代码提交信息中的应用及其争议

不同观点：
• InsideOutSanta认为没有必要在提交时保留LLM的输出，因为可以在需要时使用最合适的LLM生成信息，且此时LLM拥有更多上下文和更准确的信息。他还指出，提交信息应包含代码无法传达的内容，而不是代码本身可以展示的细节。

• pvdebbe持传统观点，认为提交信息应传达意图而非代码内容。他可能认为LLM工具的用途在于描述现有提交信息，而不是生成新的内容。

• theknarf强烈反对使用LLM生成提交信息，认为提交信息应包含代码中无法直接看到的细节，如决策原因、优缺点、相关问题链接等。

• nickcw支持theknarf的观点，强调在查看提交信息时，人们希望了解“为什么”这样做，而“什么”和“如何”做可以通过代码差异获得。如果依赖LLM工具生成提交信息，可能会缺失关键的“为什么”部分。

• alzamixer分享了一个使用LLM（如Copilot）辅助生成提交信息的脚本，展示了一种实际操作方法，表明LLM工具在某些情况下可以有效辅助开发者撰写提交信息。

• esafak补充了一个技术细节，提醒在修改提交信息时不要忘记包含代码上下文。

• infocollector关注技术实现，讨论了如何在本地运行LLM相关工具，并请求社区分享具体操作方法。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中反映出开发者对LLM在提交信息生成中的作用存在分歧，一部分人认为LLM工具能提升效率，另一部分人则担心其导致关键信息缺失。
- 传统观点与现代工具应用的碰撞，尤其是在提交信息应包含哪些内容的问题上，争议较大。
- 实际操作方法（如alzamixer的脚本分享）为LLM工具的支持者提供了具体实现路径，但仍需考虑信息完整性和准确性问题。

A cli tool written in Python that generates git commit messages using AI models

Features
Analyzes staged changes in your git repository
Generates contextual commit messages using AI
Supports multiple AI models via

Optionally edit generated commit message

pipx install acmsg

#

inputs.acmsg.url =

"
;

Add the nixpkgs overlay & include the package in your configuration
nixpkgs.overlays = [ inputs.acmsg.overlays.default ]
;
environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.acmsg ]
;

or home.packages = [ pkgs.acmsg ];

environment.systemPackages = [ inputs.acmsg.packages.
${pkgs.system}

$ nix profile install

github:quinneden/acmsg

.

data.title: The Internet 1997–2021
data.author: smusamashah
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了互联网从1997年到2021年的惊人发展，特别是通过大学项目的路由表数据展示网络增长。视频和图像记录了互联网在并购和品牌变更中的变化，重点展示了2003年和2010年的网络地图。2003年的地图首次使用颜色和图形逻辑，处理了IP地址重叠和路由循环问题。2010年的地图则首次基于BGP数据绘制，用色彩表示连接点的密集程度，曾在纽约现代艺术博物馆和《Discover》杂志上展示。这些图像直观地呈现了互联网的演变过程。

• **zetalyrae**：将标题解读为一种对过去互联网时代的悼念，暗示了标题可能引发的情感联想。

• **andrehacker**：提到1997年互联网还很小，不需要Google，用户可以通过一本1200页的"internet yellow pages"书来查找信息。他还指出，由于书本形式变得不可行，后来转向了CDROM版本，并提供了相关链接。

This image was never released publicly prior to 2014. It has only been viewable at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York, and in an edition of Discover Magazine. This is our first full Internet map with color and other graphing logic. RFC1918 addresses have been hashed into a unique checksum so they do not incorrectly overlap with other routers or hosts. data.title: Vircadia, a Bun and PostgreSQL-powered reactivity layer for games
data.author: kaliqt
data.article_summary: Vircadia 是一个高性能、开源的游戏开发平台，支持实时状态追踪和反作弊功能，利用 PostgreSQL 数据库定义游戏世界，具备事务、触发器等高级功能。开发者可以通过 WebSocket 或 HTTP 连接 API，使用 SQL 客户端直接操作游戏实体，如更新玩家数据。平台提供从原型到生产的全方位支持，具备企业级安全（OAuth 2.0）、灵活部署（容器化）、以及简化的开发流程。Vircadia 注重性能优化，去除不必要的抽象层，并且完全免费和开源，适合各类开发者使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于游戏设计工具的使用场景和技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• [reedf1] 认为该工具看起来对于软件工程师来说是直观的，并提出疑问该工具的主要使用场景是单人游戏还是多人游戏。这反映了对工具适用范围的关注，尤其是其在不同游戏类型中的应用。

• [kaliqt] 回应并详细介绍了Vircadia的重大技术更新，包括使用PostgreSQL和Bun来提升性能和减少代码膨胀。他们强调这种技术选择在游戏开发中不常见，但在这里却非常有效，能够简化管理并提升开发者体验（DX）。Kaliqt进一步说明该工具的目标是支持更多开发者创建更大规模的世界，并鼓励反馈和原型设计。此外，他们提到未来的路线图包括更多的SDK和进一步减少不必要的功能，以帮助开发者专注于游戏本身而非工具细节。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现的细节：Kaliqt详细解释了使用PostgreSQL和Bun的优势，并提到这些技术选择如何帮助提升性能和可管理性。

• 开发者支持和社区参与：Kaliqt明确表示欢迎开发者提供反馈和分享原型设计，显示出对社区参与的重视。

• 工具的未来发展方向：提到未来的技术发展计划，包括更多SDK的开发和减少不必要的功能，显示出对持续改进和优化开发者体验的承诺。

争议焦点：
• 目前讨论中没有明显的争议，但[reedf1]的提问暗示了对工具定位的某种不确定性，尤其是其在单人游戏和多人游戏开发中的具体应用场景。Kaliqt的回应虽然详细，但未直接明确该工具在单人或多人游戏开发中的偏重。

data.title: North Korean IT Workers Are Being Exposed on a Scale
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章主要揭示了一群北韩IT工人在西方公司远程工作，并将收入汇回国内支持金正恩政权。这些工人伪装成合法远程工作者，通过使用假身份或盗用身份 infiltrate 公司，参与从加密货币盗窃到为政权筹集资金的活动。文章特别提到了两名被识别的工人“Naoki Murano”和“Jenson Collins”，他们涉嫌参与了多起网络盗窃，包括从加密货币公司DeltaPrime盗取600万美元。北韩的网络活动复杂且危险，以资助政权、发展武器和收集情报为目标，与传统国家支持的黑客行为不同，更像是一个“国家认可的犯罪集团”。尽管这些工人技术娴熟，但常留下数字痕迹，如照片和网络活动记录，显示他们在奢侈生活中的享乐。文章还提到，这些工人往往自幼被选拔接受专业培训，成为黑客或开发人员。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对标题中删除“massive”一词的动机和性质的讨论

不同观点：
• The-Old-Hacker 的观点：认为删除“massive”可能是某种家长式 censorship（审查），目的是控制或限制编辑在标题中表达情感色彩。这种观点暗示了某种外部干预，可能出于政治或意识形态的原因。
   
• add-sub-mul-div 的观点：质疑“massive”一词的删除是否属于编辑上的调整，或者该词是否一开始就没有出现在网站上。这个观点更倾向于从技术角度解释，认为可能只是编辑过程中的疏漏或更正。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于删除“massive”一词的性质：The-Old-Hacker 认为这是审查，而 add-sub-mul-div 则认为可能是编辑错误或更正。
• 讨论涉及对“编辑色彩”的看法，The-Old-Hacker 认为“massive”增加了情感上的强调，删除它是为了削弱这种色彩，而 add-sub-mul-div 则没有对此作出明确判断，仅对词的存在与否提出质疑。
• 例子方面，The-Old-Hacker 提到了“paternalistic censorship”作为可能的动机，而 add-sub-mul-div 则提出了词可能一开始就不存在作为另一种解释。

The young developers
are having the time of their lives. They pop open bottles of sparkling wine, eat steak dinners, play soccer together, and lounge around in a luxurious private swimming pool, all of their activity captured in photos that were later exposed online. In one picture, a man poses in front of a life-sized
Minions
cardboard cutout. But despite their exuberance, these are not successful Silicon Valley entrepreneurs; they’re
IT workers from the Hermit Kingdom of North Korea
, who infiltrate Western companies and send their wages back home.
Two members of a cluster of North Korean developers, who allegedly operated out of Southeast Asian country Laos before being relocated to Russia by the beginning of 2024, are today being identified by researchers at cybersecurity company
DTEX
. The men, who DTEX believes have used the personas ‘Naoki Murano’ and ‘Jenson Collins,’ are alleged to have been involved in raising money for the brutalist North Korean regime as part of the widespread IT worker epidemic, with Murano alleged to have previously been
linked to a $6 million heist
at crypto firm DeltaPrime last year.
For years, Kim Jong-un’s
North Korea
has posed one of the
most
sophisticated
and
dangerous cyber
threats
to Western countries and businesses, with its hackers stealing the intellectual property needed to develop its own technology, plus looting billions in crypto to evade sanctions and
create nuclear weapons
. In February, the FBI
announced
that North Korea pulled off the biggest ever crypto heist,
stealing $1.5 billion
from crypto exchange Bybit. Alongside its skilled hackers, Pyongyang’s IT workers, who often are based in China or Russia, trick companies into employing them as remote workers and have become an
increasing menace
.
“What we’re doing isn’t working, and if it is working, it’s not working fast enough,” says Michael ‘Barni’ Barnhart, a leading North Korean cyber researcher and principal investigator at DTEX. As well as identifying Murano and Collins, DTEX, in a
detailed report about North Korean cyber activity
, is also
publishing
more than 1,000 email addresses that it alleges to have been identified as linked to North Korean IT worker activity. The move is one of the largest disclosures of North Korean IT worker activity to date.
North Korea’s broad cyber operations can’t be compared with those of other hostile nations, such as Russia and China, Barnhart explains in the DTEX report, as Pyongyang operates like a “state-sanctioned crime syndicate” rather than more traditional military or intelligence operations. Everything is driven by funding the regime, developing weaponry, and gathering information, Barnhart says. “Everything is tied together in some way, shape, or form.”
The Misfits Move In
Around 2022 and 2023, DTEX claims both Naoki Murano and Jenson Collins—their real names are not known—were based in Laos and also travelled between Vladivostok, in Russia. The pair appeared among a wider group of possible North Koreans in Laos, and a cache of their photos were first exposed in an
open Dropbox folder
. The photos were discovered by a collective of North Korean researchers who often collaborate with Barnhart and call themselves a “Misfit” alliance. In recent weeks, they’ve posted
numerous images of purported
North Korean IT workers
online.
North Korea’s IT workers are prolific in their activities, often trying to infiltrate multiple companies simultaneously by using stolen identities or creating false personas to try to appear legitimate. Some use freelance platforms; others try to
recruit international facilitators to run laptop farms
. While their online personas may be fake, the country—where millions do not have basic human rights or
access to the internet
—steers talented children into its education pipeline where they can become skilled developers and hackers. That means many of the IT workers and hackers are likely to know each other, potentially since they were children. Despite being technically adept, they often leave a trail of digital breadcrumbs in their wake.
Murano was first linked to North Korean operations publicly by cryptocurrency investigator
ZachXBT
, who published the names, cryptocurrency wallet details, and email addresses of
more than 20 North Korean IT workers
last year. Murano was then linked to the DeltaPrime heist in
reporting by Coinbase
in October.. Members of the Misfits collective have shared photos of Murano looking
pleased with himself while eating steak
and a picture of an
alleged Japanese passport
.
Meanwhile, Collins, who DTEX included in its report and who was
featured in swimming pool photos
included in the Dropbox folder, was most commonly involved in IT work that generated revenue for Pyongyang, says narcass3 a member of the Misfits who asked to be identified by their online handle. “He seems to have mainly just worked on crypto/blockchain projects, including one which seems to be completely DPR

data.title: Project West Ford
data.author: nabla9
data.article_summary:
**Project West Ford**是美国军方在1961年和1963年进行的一项实验，旨在地球上空创建人工电离层，以解决军事通信的弱点。该项目由麻省理工学院的林肯实验室负责，计划将4.8亿根铜制偶极天线放置在轨道上，形成一个环，以支持全球无线电通信。这些天线长度为1.78厘米，直径分别为25.4微米和17.8微米，设计用于反射8 GHz的信号。

1961年的首次尝试失败，天线未能散开，但1963年的第二次尝试成功实现了通信传输。然而，由于现代通信卫星的发展和国际科学界的抗议，该项目最终被搁置。英国天文学家和皇家天文学会等对实验提出反对，认为其造成了空间碎片。抗议促使1967年的《外层空间条约》增加了协商条款。尽管大部分天线在几年内脱离轨道，但仍有一些未正确散开的天线残留在轨道上，截至2023年4月，仍有44簇天线在轨道上。

Project West Ford
(also known as

and

) was a test carried out by
Massachusetts Institute of Technology
's
Lincoln Laboratory
on behalf of the
United States military
in 1961 and 1963 to create an artificial
ionosphere
above the Earth.
[
1
]
This was done to solve a major weakness that had been identified in military communications.
[
2

History
[
edit
]
At the height of the
Cold War
, all international communications were either sent through
submarine communications cables
or bounced off the natural
ionosphere
. The United States military was concerned that the
Soviets
might cut those cables, forcing the unpredictable ionosphere to be the only means of communication with overseas forces.
[
1
]
To mitigate the potential threat,
Walter E. Morrow
started Project Needles at the MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1958. The goal of the project was to place a ring of 480,000,000
[
3
]
[
4

copper

in orbit to facilitate global
radio
communication. The dipoles collectively provided passive support to Project West Ford's
parabolic dish
(located at the
Haystack Observatory
in the
town of Westford
) to communicate with distant sites.
The needles used in the experiment were 1.78 centimetres (0.70 in) long and 25.4
micrometres
(1.00
thou
) [1961] or 17.8 micrometres (0.70 thou) [1963] in diameter.
[
5

The length was chosen because it was half the
wavelength
of the 8
GHz
signal used in the study.

1

The needles were placed in
medium Earth orbit
at an altitude of between 3,500 and 3,800 kilometres (2,200–2,400 mi) at inclinations of 96 and 87 degrees.

A first attempt was launched on 21 October 1961,

during which the needles failed to disperse.

data.title: The Cryptography Behind Passkeys
data.author: tatersolid
data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要介绍了密码学中的身份验证，特别是通过加密技术实现的更安全的用户认证方式——** passkeys（通行密钥）**。虽然加密通常让人想到加密保密，但身份验证同样重要。传统的密码容易受到钓鱼攻击和数据泄露的威胁，而passkeys通过加密技术提供更强的安全性。

**Passkey的加密基础**是基于公私钥对的数字签名。注册时，网站保存公钥和标识符；验证时，网站提供挑战并等待包含该挑战的签名响应。由于服务器仅保存公钥，且用户不发送敏感信息，即使服务器被黑客攻击也不会泄露敏感数据。

然而，**WebAuthn** 规范通过绑定来源（origin binding）解决了钓鱼问题。浏览器将请求的来源传递给认证器，认证器只在请求来源与创建passkey的网站匹配时使用密钥对，从而防止钓鱼攻击。此外，WebAuthn只允许使用HTTPS的来源，确保请求来自具有有效证书的服务器。

**认证器类型**包括硬件或软件，可以验证用户的存在，某些还可以结合“用户所知”进行多因素认证。

总结来说，passkeys通过加密技术及WebAuthn规范实现了一种防钓鱼的强身份验证机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Passkeys技术的优缺点及其应用场景

不同观点：
• **Whartung的观点**：质疑Passkeys在不同设备和操作系统之间切换时的表现，特别是当不进行密码同步时，密码恢复功能的有效性如何保障。该评论对跨设备使用的便利性和密码恢复的可靠性提出了疑问。

• **Labadal的观点**：对Passkeys的便利性和安全性表示赞赏，特别是生物识别技术的使用，但同时对供应商锁定（vendor lock-in）问题表示担忧，并询问Passkeys标准的现状及未来解决方案。

• **Andrewmcwatters的观点**：认为传统的密码和密码管理器已经足够好，尤其是TOTP支持广泛。对Passkeys持怀疑态度，认为它是大型科技公司用来锁定用户的技术，缺乏便携性，尤其是缺乏导出和导入的支持。对一些人为大公司辩护的态度感到不满。

• **Joelthelion的观点**：对Passkeys的实际应用情况提出疑问，质疑其是否得到了广泛应用和接受。

• **Solarkraft的观点**：认为挑战-响应（challenge-response）加非对称加密是理想的身份验证方式，例如SSH。对Passkeys的实现方式表示不满，指出其缺乏备份和互操作性差的问题，并通过个人经历说明在Mac上使用Firefox创建Passkeys时遇到的困难。

补充讨论：
• **供应商锁定问题**：Labadal和Andrewmcwatters都提到了供应商锁定问题，这是Passkeys应用中的一个重要争议点。
• **跨设备使用和密码恢复**：Whartung和Solarkraft都提到了Passkeys在跨设备使用中的问题，包括操作复杂性和失败情况。
• **技术便携性和互操作性**：Andrewmcwatters和Solarkraft都对Passkeys的便携性和互操作性提出了批评，认为其在这些方面存在不足。

争议焦点：Passkeys的供应商锁定问题、跨设备使用和密码恢复的可靠性、技术便携性和互操作性是主要争议点。这些问题的存在使得一些用户对Passkeys技术的实际应用持怀疑态度。

43983159.article_content:
When most people think of cryptography, the first thing they typically think of is encryption: keeping information confidential. But just as important (if not more) is authenticity: ensuring that information is really coming from an authentic source. When you visit a website, the server typically proves its identity through a Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate authenticated by the Web Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). Passwords are the traditional solution for user authentication, but they suffer from phishing attacks and data breaches. This is where passkeys come in.
Instead of explaining what passkeys are and why they are better than passwords—
something
many
other
resources
have already covered—this post will examine the cryptography behind passkeys, the guarantees they do or do not give, and interesting cryptographic things you can do with them, such as generating cryptographic keys and storing certificates. You need to understand the cryptography behind passkeys to implement secure authentication correctly. We’ll also discuss the main passkey specification, WebAuthn, and show you how to use extensions of passkey mechanisms to build a more intricate system with different capabilities.
Passkey cryptography basics
At their core, passkeys are just key pairs used to produce digital signatures. When registering a passkey, the website saves the public key and an identifier. When authenticating a user via a passkey, the website provides a challenge and waits for a signed response including this challenge (and some other metadata, such as the identifier). The identifier is used to look up the public key, which is used to verify the signature.
From a cryptographic perspective, this is quite straightforward. The private key authenticates the user, but no sensitive information useful to an attacker is communicated to the server. If the server challenge is properly generated—e.g., as a uniformly random sequence of 32 bytes—then it will prevent replay attacks. Since the server holds only a public key and the user does not send it sensitive information, there is nothing to be leaked in case of a hack.
But digital signatures alone aren’t enough to solve the phishing problem. If we stopped here with just the cryptographic primitives, users would still be vulnerable. For instance, without additional safeguards, an attacker might trick users into signing challenges for the wrong website or reusing the same key pair across multiple sites.
This is why passkeys are built on the
W3C’s WebAuthn
specification, which adds crucial security properties beyond the basic cryptography. Let’s look at how WebAuthn transforms these simple cryptographic primitives into a phishing-resistant authentication system.
WebAuthn
WebAuthn is the main specification behind passkeys. In simple terms, users access a
website
(relying party) through their
browser
(WebAuthn user agent) on a
device
such as a laptop, phone, or PC (client device). The browser interacts with an
authenticator
, a piece of hardware or software that generates the passkey key pair, and creates digital signatures using this key pair.
Figure 1: Simplified view of a passkey authentication flow.
In the diagram above, you can see how a passkey authentication works:
The website requests authentication through the browser.
The browser communicates with the authenticator.
The authenticator checks credentials and user presence.
The authenticator returns a signed response.
The browser forwards this response to the website for verification.
(This interaction between browser and authenticator is described in more detail in another specification: the FIDO Alliance’s
Client to Authenticator Protocol
(CTAP).) This is a simplified description; the WebAuthn specification allows for a larger variety of use cases (e.g., everything could work via a mobile application instead of a website/browser). However, those specifics are not relevant to understanding how passkeys work with cryptography.
Anti-phishing protections
WebAuthn solves the phishing problem through origin binding. The specification requires browsers to provide the
origin
of the request (i.e., the website domain) to the authenticator. The authenticator in turn uses passkeys only when the website making the request matches the website that created the passkey.
This means that if you create a passkey for bank.com, a phishing site at fake-bank.com simply cannot use it—your authenticator will refuse the request. Each website also gets its own unique key pair, eliminating the password reuse problem entirely.
Additionally, the specification allows only origins that use HTTPS, which means that the request comes from a server that has a valid certificate for the corresponding origin.
Types of authenticators
Generally, authenticators are “something you have.” All authenticators can check whether a user is actually present when authenticating. Some authenticators can additionally verify the user according to “something they know,” such as

这篇文章简要介绍了密码学中的身份验证，特别是通过加密技术实现的更安全的用户认证方式——** passkeys（通行密钥）**。虽然加密通常让人想到加密保密，但身份验证同样重要。传统的密码容易受到钓鱼攻击和数据泄露的威胁，而passkeys通过加密技术提供更强的安全性。

**Passkey的加密基础**是基于公私钥对的数字签名。注册时，网站保存公钥和标识符；验证时，网站提供挑战并等待包含该挑战的签名响应。由于服务器仅保存公钥，且用户不发送敏感信息，即使服务器被黑客攻击也不会泄露敏感数据。

然而，**WebAuthn** 规范通过绑定来源（origin binding）解决了钓鱼问题。浏览器将请求的来源传递给认证器，认证器只在请求来源与创建passkey的网站匹配时使用密钥对，从而防止钓鱼攻击。此外，WebAuthn只允许使用HTTPS的来源，确保请求来自具有有效证书的服务器。

**认证器类型**包括硬件或软件，可以验证用户的存在，某些还可以结合“用户所知”进行多因素认证。

总结来说，passkeys通过加密技术及WebAuthn规范实现了一种防钓鱼的强身份验证机制。

不同观点：
• **Whartung的观点**：质疑Passkeys在不同设备和操作系统之间切换时的表现，特别是当不进行密码同步时，密码恢复功能的有效性如何保障。该评论对跨设备使用的便利性和密码恢复的可靠性提出了疑问。

• **Labadal的观点**：对Passkeys的便利性和安全性表示赞赏，特别是生物识别技术的使用，但同时对供应商锁定（vendor lock-in）问题表示担忧，并询问Passkeys标准的现状及未来解决方案。

• **Andrewmcwatters的观点**：认为传统的密码和密码管理器已经足够好，尤其是TOTP支持广泛。对Passkeys持怀疑态度，认为它是大型科技公司用来锁定用户的技术，缺乏便携性，尤其是缺乏导出和导入的支持。对一些人为大公司辩护的态度感到不满。

主要讨论点：HDR技术在摄影和显示设备中的应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **HDR显示的实用性问题**：  
  - [gyomu] 认为HDR内容在社交媒体上的显示效果过于刺眼，尤其是在夜间或低亮度环境下使用时，体验较差。相比之下，全屏HDR内容（如游戏和电影）则表现较好。
  - [CarVac] 同样认为当前的HDR显示不舒服，尤其是当亮度过高时，如室内照片中的白墙被显示得过于明亮。

• **HDR技术实现与色彩管理问题**：  
  - [mxfh] 批评文章未深入讨论消费级数字环境下的色彩管理问题，并指出用户界面在HDR下未经过充分测试，可能导致字幕等内容过于刺眼。同时提到Dolby Vision和Apple在封闭平台上的领先地位，而开放网络环境中的HDR仍不成熟。
  - [the__alchemist] 认为HDR技术的潜在价值毋庸置疑，可以显著提升视觉体验，但过去由于市场未成熟，HDR显示器未普及，如今可能值得重新考虑购买。

• **技术细节与实现方法的争议**：  
  - [sergioisidoro] 提到在模拟摄影中，通过显影剂的补偿作用可以达到更高的动态范围，而不仅仅是通过遮挡和燃烧技术。同时批评手机上的HDR功能虽然适合记录家庭时刻，但不适合作为创意工具。
  - [tomatotomato37] 提供了更多技术资料链接，建议对HDR技术感兴趣的读者深入了解。

• **浏览器兼容性问题**：  
  - [echo_time] 指出在Firefox浏览器上查看相关内容时遇到困惑，而在Chrome浏览器上则体验更好，怀疑Firefox缺少某些设置。
  - [sebstefan] 提到在Firefox的画中画模式下，某些设计问题得以解决，但文章中的特定演示未触发画中画选项。

• **HDR技术的市场接受度与技术门槛**：  
  - [aidenn0] 指出HDR和4K显示的普及面临巨大的基础设施升级成本，消费者可能需要很长时间才能完全接受这些新技术。
  - [bookofjoe] 代表普通用户表示对技术细节不感兴趣，只希望设备开箱即用，不愿意手动调整各种设置。

• **HDR技术的支持与期待**：  
  - [randall] 表示对文章和HDR效果的赞赏，特别是HDR照片展示令他印象深刻。
  - [c-fe] 虽然对当前的HDR内容持怀疑态度，但期待某些摄影应用（如Halide）能带来更好的HDR体验。

补充讨论：
• **HDR与亮度的关系**：  
  - [perching_aix] 提到显示器的亮度输出与自然光不同，即便自然光亮度更高，显示器上的高亮内容仍可能刺眼。同时指出HDR与高亮度是两个不同的概念，HDR只是一种表示方式，高亮度并非HDR的必要条件。

• **相机动态范围问题**：  
  - [fogleman] 质疑文章未解释清楚相机在动态范围不足的情况下如何通过单次曝光实现HDR效果。

争议焦点：
• HDR技术的实际用户体验与技术实现之间的矛盾，尤其是在非全屏应用（如日常计算和网页浏览）中，HDR显示的舒适性和色彩管理问题。

data.title: How the economics of multitenancy work
data.author: tsaifu
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Blacksmith如何通过多租户经济模式实现盈利，特别是在处理CI（持续集成）工作负载方面的独特优势。CI工作负载具有高度不稳定和短暂的特性，通常在工作时间出现高峰，而非全天候运行。这种不规则性使得传统硬件管理变得不切实际，而Blacksmith的serverless CI云平台则通过资源池化和按需计费，解决了这一问题。

Blacksmith使用数百台裸金属游戏CPU，通过Firecracker技术在需求出现时快速启动微虚拟机，任务完成后立即销毁。由于这些硬件成本是固定的，Blacksmith的关键在于提高利用率。通过吸引多个客户，他们能够平滑高峰需求，将原本的资源浪费转化为持续的收入。随着客户数量增加，CI任务的随机性逐渐形成一个可预测的模式，从而最大化资源利用率和利润。这种模式不仅为客户提供了灵活性，也确保了Blacksmith的可持续盈利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多租户架构下的资源分配与成本效率问题，特别是在CI/CD管道和云计算环境中的应用。

不同观点：
• [zdc1] 支持动态CPU分配，认为这样可以解决客户在CPU资源利用率低时仍需支付高额费用的问题。他还提到CI供应商可以通过统计数据优化资源调度，提高资源利用率，从而实现更高的经济效益。

• [Havoc] 认为固定租赁模式不如结合基础固定资源和高峰时使用竞价实例的模式高效，后者可以在成本上更具优势。

• [TuringTest] 从历史角度出发，指出当前的多租户概念类似于过去的“分时”概念，认为技术发展往往是旧概念的新应用。

• [coolcase] 分享了在工作中通过将多个服务打包到Kubernetes集群中以平滑资源峰值和降低成本的经验，认为这种方法不仅能减少浪费，还能利用云中的预留实例和折扣来控制成本。

• [mlhpdx] 认为多租户SaaS供应商希望成本成为使用量的次线性函数，通过大容量单元分配小工作单元的方式实现成本效率。然而，这种模式在低量时是阶梯式增长的，只有在达到大规模时才显现出线性增长的优势，因此在公司增长阶段特别有利。

• [shadowgovt] 关注客户端的体验，指出无服务器架构可能带来的前端延迟问题，特别是在开发周期的紧循环中，这种延迟可能非常痛苦。不过，他也提到如果峰值是规律性的，高级无服务器系统可以通过历史数据预测并提前准备资源。

• [0xbadcafebee] 简要总结认为，这种案例实际上是关于资源打包问题，而在其他业务案例中，多租户的经济性更多与人力成本和组织成本的效率有关，而非仅仅是计算效率。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何在多租户环境中平衡资源利用率和客户体验。特别是在无服务器架构中，延迟问题是一个需要解决的重要挑战。
• 动态资源分配和利用历史数据预测资源需求是提升资源利用效率的重要手段。
• 不同观点中都提到了成本控制的重要性，但实现方式各有侧重，包括动态分配、竞价实例、打包技术和预留实例等。

How The Economics of Multitenancy Work
Aditya Jayaprakash
May 13, 2025
In the early days of Blacksmith, back when we were just a scrappy
YC startup
building a serverless cloud platform for CI workloads, we ran simulations to model our margins. We figured that with enough customers, the math would work out, and we crossed our fingers â but we didnât have any real-world data to back up our predictions.
About six months after we launched, I came across
a blog post
by Marc Brooker on the economics of multitenant systems. It captured what we were trying to do much more elegantly than the half-formed ideas in our heads. This post was heavily inspired by Marcâs, and reading it was a real moment of,
"Oh! someone else has thought about this, and it makes sense."
Now, weâre running thousands of jobs every minute and millions every month, and itâs been exciting to actually see this play out at scale and watch the math work in real life. Yet, people still often ask in disbelief how we actually make money from our setup â are we just burning sweet VC dollars with no return for them in sight? So, for the non-believers and anyone who is just a little bit curious, letâs take a peek behind the curtain and dive into how the economics of multitenancy work â using ourselves as a case study.
CI Isnât Like Production (And That Matters).
Unlike production workloads, CI workloads tend to be very spiky. Below, weâve plotted CPU utilization for one of our customers over a 24-hour window. It spikes when someone pushes code, then chills out in between.
This customer runs 35 jobs on 16 vCPU machines for every git push, meaning they need over 500 vCPUs every time they run CI. See where the chart flatlines like a patient on the George Clooney classic âERâ? Since their team is split across the US and EU, thereâs an 8-hour stretch in the middle with zero usage. And when a few engineers push at once â say, five people â they suddenly need 2,500+ vCPUs instantly. And all these CI jobs are short-lived. Most CI jobs finish fast (relatively speaking), somewhere between 5 and 40 minutes. All of these chaotic characteristics of CI workloads might sound like a nightmare, but itâs actually a perfect fit for the serverless model weâve built our platform around, and most importantly, for our customers.
Why Our Serverless CI Model Works.
Think about it from the customer's side: If you need 2,500 vCPUs at peak, it would be crazy to buy and manage all that hardware yourself â especially when it would sit idle most of the time. But with Blacksmithâs serverless CI cloud, you get to borrow from our pool and only pay for what you use. Spiky, bursty, chaotic? No problem.Â
Whatâs more, CI traffic is highly predictable. Developers are pushing code during work hours, not at 2AM or during holiday weekends. Unlike some production workloads, our fleet is not bracing for Black Friday-style traffic surges â and that shapes a lot of how we built it.
Our Fleet: What It Looks Like and What Matters Most.
We have a fleet of hundreds of bare-metal gaming CPUs that weâre virtualizing over â when a customer needs to run a CI job, we spin up a microVM using
Firecracker
, and once the jobâs complete â poof! Itâs gone.Â
Each of our machines has 32 vCPUs, and across the whole kit and kaboodle, we manage tens of thousands of vCPUs across our region us-west and eu-central. We pin customers to one region for consistency and workflow support.
Currently, we lease these machines for a fixed period. Soon, weâll be racking them up in a datacenter. Regardless, these machines are a fixed cost â whether we have customers or not, weâre still paying for them. So, the name of the CI cost optimization game is utilization. If theyâre barely used, our margins are low; if theyâre used enough, we make that cash money. The metric we track the most is average fleet utilization â and thatâs where customer chaos becomes our secret weapon.
A Bit of Chaos is Bad. A Lot of Chaos? Chef's Kiss.
Letâs say we only had one customer â the one from earlier who needs 2,500 vCPUs at peak. Weâd need around 80 machines to handle that load, but for most of the day, those machines would just sit there, twiddling their thumbs. Weâd be bleeding money.
Now, add a second customer in the same time zone. Their CI jobs donât peak at the exact same time, so instead of needing 160 machines (80 + 80), we might only need 110 to cover both. As we add more customers, the effect compounds. We add even more customers, and all the random bursts of activity start to blend together.
Over time, CI jobs start behaving like a Poisson process â random, short bursts spread out across time. From a distance, what once looked like sharp spikes from individual customers smooths into a predictable pattern. The more customers we

• [coolcase] 分享了在工作中通过将多个服务打包到Kubernetes集群中以平滑资源峰值和降低成本的经验，认为这种方法不仅能减少浪费，还能利用云中的预留实例和折扣来控制成本。

• [mlhpdx] 认为多租户SaaS供应商希望成本成为使用量的次线性函数，通过大容量单元分配小工作单元的方式实现成本效率。然而，这种模式在低量时是阶梯式增长的，只有在达到大规模时才显现出线性增长的优势，因此在公司增长阶段特别有利。

• [shadowgovt] 关注客户端的体验，指出无服务器架构可能带来的前端延迟问题，特别是在开发周期的紧循环中，这种延迟可能非常痛苦。不过，他也提到如果峰值是规律性的，高级无服务器系统可以通过历史数据预测并提前准备资源。

• [0xbadcafebee] 简要总结认为，这种案例实际上是关于资源打包问题，而在其他业务案例中，多租户的经济性更多与人力成本和组织成本的效率有关，而非仅仅是计算效率。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何在多租户环境中平衡资源利用率和客户体验。特别是在无服务器架构中，延迟问题是一个需要解决的重要挑战。
• 动态资源分配和利用历史数据预测资源需求是提升资源利用效率的重要手段。
• 不同观点中都提到了成本控制的重要性，但实现方式各有侧重，包括动态分配、竞价实例、打包技术和预留实例等。

data.title: Breaking the Sound Barrier Part I: Fuzzing CoreAudio with Mach Messages
data.author: MajesticHobo2
data.article_summary: 本文由Google高级安全工程师Dillon Franke撰写，介绍了他在macOS系统上通过Mach IPC消息进行安全研究的过程。作者聚焦于使用Mach IPC消息作为攻击向量，寻找和利用沙箱逃逸漏洞，特别是coreaudiod系统守护进程中的类型混淆漏洞。他采用了一种名为“知识驱动模糊测试”的混合方法，结合了模糊测试与手动逆向工程，以快速测试大量输入并识别系统行为异常。作者开发了一个自定义模糊测试工具，并详细描述了整个研究过程，包括选择目标、创建测试工具、分析崩溃和代码覆盖率等步骤。他还提到了一些历史上的相关研究，例如Ian Beer在2016年发现的XNU内核问题。最终，作者公开了他的模糊测试工具及相关代码，希望为其他macOS安全研究人员提供参考。

43950693.article_content:
Guest post by Dillon Franke, Senior Security Engineer
,
20% time on Project Zero
Every second, highly-privileged MacOS system daemons accept and process hundreds of IPC messages. In some cases, these message handlers accept data from sandboxed or unprivileged processes.
In this blog post, I’ll explore using Mach IPC messages as an attack vector to find and exploit sandbox escapes. I’ll detail how I used a custom fuzzing harness, dynamic instrumentation, and plenty of debugging/static analysis to identify a high-risk type confusion vulnerability in the
coreaudiod
system daemon. Along the way, I’ll discuss some of the difficulties and tradeoffs I
encountered
.
Transparently,
this was my first venture into the world of MacOS security research and
building a custom fuzzing harness. I hope this post serves as a guide to those who wish to embark on similar research endeavors.
I am open-sourcing the fuzzing harness I built, as well as several tools I wrote that were useful to me throughout this project. All of this can be found here:
https://github.com/googleprojectzero/p0tools/tree/master/CoreAudioFuzz
The Approach: Knowledge-Driven Fuzzing
For this research project, I adopted a hybrid approach that combined fuzzing and manual reverse engineering, which I refer to as
knowledge-driven fuzzing
. This method, learned from my friend
Ned Williamson
, balances automation with targeted investigation. Fuzzing provided the means to quickly test a wide range of inputs and identify areas where the system’s behavior deviated from expectations. However, when the fuzzer’s code coverage plateaued or specific hurdles arose, manual analysis came into play, forcing me to dive deeper into the target’s inner workings.
Knowledge-driven fuzzing offers two key advantages. First, the research process never stagnates, as the goal of improving the code coverage of the fuzzer is always present. Second, achieving this goal requires a deep understanding of the code you are fuzzing. By the time you begin triaging legitimate, security-relevant crashes, the reverse engineering process will have given you extensive knowledge of the codebase, enabling analysis of crashes from an informed perspective.
The cycle I followed during this research is as follows:
Identify an att
ack vector
Choose a target
Create a fuzzing harness
Fuzz and produce crashes
Analyze crashes and code coverage
Iterate on the fuzzing harness
Repeat steps 4-6
Identify an Attack Vector
Standard browser sandboxing limits code execution by restricting direct operating system access. Consequently, exploiting a browser vulnerability typically requires the use of a separate “sandbox escape” vulnerability.
Since interprocess communication (IPC) mechanisms allow two processes to communicate with each other, they can naturally serve as a bridge from a sandboxed process to an unrestricted one. This makes them a prime attack vector for sandbox escapes, as shown below.
I chose Mach messages, the lowest level IPC component in the MacOS operating system, as the attack vector of focus for this research. I chose them mostly due to my desire to understand MacOS IPC mechanisms at their most core level, as well as the track record of historical security issues with Mach messages.
Previous Work and Background
Leveraging Mach messages in exploit chains is far from a novel idea. For example, Ian Beer
identified a core design issue
in 2016 with the XNU kernel related to the handling of
task_t
Mach ports, which allowed for exploitation via Mach messages.
Another post
showed how an in-the-wild exploit chain
utilized Mach messages in 2019 for heap grooming techniques.
I also drew much inspiration from Ret2 Systems’
blog post
about leveraging Mach message handlers to find and weaponize a Safari sandbox escape.
I won’t spend too much time detailing the ins and outs of how Mach messages work, (that is better left to a more
comprehensive post
on the subject) but here’s a brief overview of Mach IPC for this blog post:
Mach messages are stored within kernel-managed message queues, represented by a Mach port
A process can fetch a message from a given port if it holds the receive right for
that port
A process can send a message to a given port if it holds a send right to that port
MacOS applications can register a service with the bootstrap server, a special mach port which all processes have a send right to by default. This allows other processes to send a Mach message to the bootstrap server inquiring about a specific service, and the bootstrap server can respond with a send right
to that service’s Mach port
. MacOS system daemons register Mach services via
launchd
. You can view their
.plist
files within the
/System/Library/LaunchAgents
and
/System/Library/LaunchDaemons
directories to get an idea of the services registered. For example, the
.plist
file below highlights a Mach service registered for the Address Book application on MacOS using the identifier
com.apple.AddressBook.AssistantService
.
<?xml

data.title: SMS 2FA is not just insecure, it's also hostile to mountain people
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章描述了一位住在北卡罗来纳州山区的年长女士面临的困境：尽管她学会了使用智能手机和Signal群聊，但许多网站使用SMS双因素认证（2FA），而由于她所在地区的手机信号差，她无法接收这些验证码。即使开启了WiFi通话功能，SMS验证码仍无法接收，因为短码信息不支持WiFi通话。她不得不列出所有被锁定的网站，然后前往城镇与朋友会面，逐一将它们转换为TOTP 2FA，但并非所有网站都支持此功能。其他解决方案如更换VOIP服务或安装信号增强器都过于复杂和昂贵。文章指出，山区有数百万人面临类似问题，虽然有互联网，但手机服务差，使得简单的登录操作变得困难重重。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何解决在接收短信（尤其是2FA验证码）方面遇到的问题，特别是在信号不好或技术限制的情况下。

不同观点：
• _hyn3认为，用户可以直接联系公司，要求不要向特定号码发送短信，或者完全移除电话号码。同时建议加强其他安全措施，如使用强密码。
• lxgr提出将手机号码转到支持通过WiFi接收短信的VOIP提供商，但指出某些公司因安全原因不支持向VOIP号码发送短信。此外，提到WiFi通话功能在接收普通短信方面有效，但对2FA码无效。
• LeifCarrotson建议使用微型基站（femtocell）解决信号问题，特别是在偏远地区或信号死角。并分享了在工作场所通过安装多个微型基站解决信号问题的实际经验。
• dreamcompiler提供了三种解决方案：使用Google Voice、获取微型基站、以及通过mightytext在电脑上接收短信，但指出某些方案可能因技术限制或成本问题并不适合所有人。
• marssaxman分享了自己在信号不好的地区生活时的经验，通过开车到信号好的地方接收2FA码，但认为这不是理想的长期解决方案。
• brettanomyces讨论了TOTP、PUSH和PASSKEYS等不同的认证方式，指出TOTP在某些场景下的局限性，PUSH需要安装多个应用程序，而PASSKEYS虽然是一个有前景的解决方案，但尚未普及。
• vanburen建议使用4G路由器和专用SIM卡接收2FA短信，并通过路由器将短信转发到电子邮件，特别是在某些区域信号不好的情况下。
• Neywiny提到在使用共享交通工具时因技术问题无法结束行程的经历，反映了过度依赖手机和2FA可能带来的不便。
• jboggan分享了在偏远地区无法接收Coinbase的2FA短信的经历，最终只能手写IOU解决问题。
• Meleagris同意其他人的观点，并提出了创建SMS代理服务的想法，以帮助那些无法接收2FA短信的人。
• modeless推荐使用Google Fi，因为它可以在WiFi上接收所有类型的2FA短信，包括短码，并且不需要手机开机。
• hkchad提到通过Verizon获得Fem2Cell解决了家中信号不好的问题，但只影响发送大文件。
• headora建议更换手机服务提供商，并指出自己通过WiFi接收2FA短信从未遇到问题，同时认为2FA短信认证方式本身并不理想。
• zkms指出WiFi通话功能可以解决接收普通短信的问题，并提供了苹果支持链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是2FA通过短信的方式是否可靠和安全，许多人认为这不是理想的解决方案。
• 不同的技术方案（如VOIP、微型基站、Google Voice等）各有优缺点，适用性取决于具体情况和地区。
• 用户在信号不好的地区如何接收2FA码是一个普遍存在的问题，涉及实际操作中的多种不便和潜在解决方案。
• 讨论中多次提到公司对VOIP号码和2FA码的限制，反映了技术实现与安全考虑之间的矛盾。

43984297.article_content:
SMS 2FA is not just insecure, it's also hostile to mountain people
May 14, 2025
i have a friend — she's an old lady born and raised here in the western north carolina mountains. she hates computers, yes, but she's been willing to learn a lot and quickly after joining a big signal group chat that our shared local community uses to keep in touch.
aside from memeing with the best of them in the group chat, she also maintains a large fish pond outside the house she built herself. this despite being in her 70s. she's an inspiration.
she has a landline. it works great, and the landline phone hardware works great with her hearing aids. she's had it for years. spectrum has a monoply in our area so the landline and her cable internet service is with spectrum.
she got a cell phone a few years ago. she got a smartphone basically because she had to to do basic life tasks, including joining the big signal group chat. at first she just used it on wifi, but quickly she decided she wanted to be able to use the phone everywhere so she got a cell phone plan from spectrum because they were already her ISP. spectrum mobile uses the verizon network — famed for its good rural coverage.
this is where things started to go haywire.
all her accounts on websites, things like email and bank accounts and health insurance and healthcare providers, they started trying to send her SMS messages in order to let her get into her accounts.
the SMS codes don't work, because they don't come. she doesn't have cell service at her house. it's up in the mountains, sure, but it's not
isolated
. she lives 20 minutes from downtown asheville and she has lots of neighbors on her road.
she turned on wifi calling on her phone. now she could receive SMS messages from friends and family, but 2FA codes still weren't coming through. i did some digging, and it turns out messages from 5 digit shortcodes often aren't supported over wifi calling. sometimes they are, but in her case they're clearly not. she has a current, stock iphone. she's using the spectrum-provided internet hardware. she knows how to use her phone.
i did more digging — it turns out some ISP-provided landline services support receiving SMS messages to the landline, and then a computer voice reads them out to you. “we don't offer that service” the spectrum chat told us.
some of these accounts can likely be converted to using TOTP 2FA rather than SMS 2FA. this is good, but you have to get in to begin with in order to turn that on. so what my friend has to do is:
make a list, over time, of the websites that she's locked out of because of SMS 2FA
not be able to use those sites at home the whole time she's making the list
schedule a meetup with a friend like me
drive to town to meet the friend
sit down and systematically go through the list of websites and convert them to TOTP
inevitably discover that some of them don't support TOTP
try and contact those companies and explain that they need to turn off SMS 2FA on her account so that she can use their healthcare/banking/email/whatever service from her home
discover that it's not possible to talk to a company anymore in 2025
other options available to her include
port her cellphone number to a VOIP provider that does support receiving SMS from shortcodes over wifi
spend hundreds of dollars setting up a cell tower signal booster outside her house
move
these are all ridiculous options that shouldn't be necessary in order to log in to a website.
if you look at the spectrum mobile coverage map where my friend lives, it shows she has perfect coverage at her house. and all her neighbors do too. all the way up the holler in fact!
this is simply false. she usually doesn't even have service 100 meters down the road.
another friend of mine who also lives out in the county, a millenial, once said that “SMS 2FA is the bane of [her] existence.” the valley she's in isn't even that deep.
and TOTP, the obvious alternative solution, is still pretty sorry. you have to download an app to do it, it's not just a capability that a phone has by default. and then when trying to find an app to use for it, you're presented with a multitude of high-stakes choices, and often pretty technical explanations if you start internet searching about which app to use.
i understand why SMS 2FA is so ubiquitous. when it works, the UX is good, nontechnical users intuitively understand it, and it's usually secure
enough
.
but there are 1.1
million
people in these western north carolina mountains, 25 million in the rest of the appalachians, and many millions more in the mountain west and pacific ranges.
we have internet, but we have F-tier cell service — what are we supposed to do?

• [philipallstar] 认为提高通行速度对负担得起通行费的人来说是好处，强调了收费道路的普遍好处。

data.title: FlowG – Distributed Systems without raft (part 2)
data.author: linkdd
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了FlowG分布式系统中不使用Raft协议的复制方案。通过采用SWIM协议（Gossip协议的一种）实现节点发现，并利用Hashicorp的memberlist库进行集群成员管理与故障检测。选择HTTP作为传输层替代TCP/UDP，便于添加TLS和认证，并支持反向代理和未来可能的HTTP3升级。

FlowG采用BadgerDB作为存储后端，利用其版本控制和增量备份功能实现数据复制，避免了使用操作日志。对于不同存储类型（auth、config、log），分别采用"最后写入为准"和"仅追加"策略，自然实现了CRDT的效果。

复制过程通过SWIM协议和BadgerDB的增量备份功能实现，节点间定期交换状态并通过HTTP请求同步数据。当前方案仍处于实验阶段，还需进一步测试以应对同步失败、网络分区和节点故障等情况。

43983385.article_content:
Distributed Systems without Raft (part 2)
David Delassus
Follow
5 min read
·
Just now
--
Listen
Share
Part 1: SWIM Protocol for Node Discovery
Part 2: Incremental updates of every node
Introduction and Context
Recently, I published the
v0.37.0
release of
FlowG
, a Free and OpenSource low-code log processing software:
FlowG
Free and Open-Source Low-Code log processing solution
link-society.github.io
FlowG’s pipeline editor
FlowG’s log viewer
This version includes the first
experimental
draft of replication, allowing FlowG to run on multiple servers as a single “semantic” instance.
Refresher on Node Discovery
We chose a
Gossip
protocol,
SWIM
(
Scalable Weakly Consistent Infection-style Process Group Membership):
GitHub - hashicorp/memberlist: Golang package for gossip based membership and failure detection
Golang package for gossip based membership and failure detection - hashicorp/memberlist
github.com
Thanks to this library, we can tell a node to “join” another node, they will start exchanging information about the cluster architecture (aka: known nodes of the cluster).
A technical choice was also to use HTTP as the transport layer instead of the default TCP/UDP:
the TCP part is replaced by a hijacked HTTP connection (similar to Websocket);
the UDP part is replaced by normal HTTP requests.
“Why?” you may ask. Here are a few reasons:
it becomes easy to add TLS, authentication, etc;
Reverse Proxies are easy to setup;
we might explore using HTTP3 later on if performance becomes an issue.
Eventual Consistency
As said in the original article, we chose for FlowG to be
eventually consistent
. We initially planned to use an “operation log” and
C
onflict-free
R
eplicated
D
ata
T
ypes
(CRDTs) to implement the replication part.
This idea was temporarily dismissed. I’ll explain why.
Our storage backend is
BadgerDB
:
Overview - Badger
Welcome to the Badger docs!
docs.hypermode.com
It is an embeddable key/value database with full transaction support. Internally, it uses a
Log Structured Merge Tree
(LSM) to organize key/value pairs.
Every key/value pair is assigned a “version”, and every mutation on a key updates that version. This enables incremental backups quite easily:
nextSince, err := db.Backup(writer, since)
nextSince, err = db.Backup(writer, nextSince + 1)
// ...
This also means that we don’t actually
need
an “operation log” to track the mutations done on a database.
As for the CRDT, FlowG has 3 kinds of storages:
auth:
stores users, permissions, tokens, roles, …
config:
stores configuration (pipelines, transformers, forwarders, …)
log:
stores actual logs
The first 2 storages aren’t used that much. FlowG is a “setup&forget” kind of software. The 3rd one is
append-only
(in reality, we also have a purge operation to remove logs, but we never update logs).
The BadgerDB instance for those storage already acts like a CRDT. It is “last write wins” for the
auth
and
config
storages, and “append-only” for the
log
storage.
Actual Replication
To implement replication, we will rely on the SWIM protocol, and on BadgerDB’s incremental backup feature.
The
hashicorp/memberlist
package provides what they call a “TCP Push/Pull”. Periodically, each node computes their local state, send them to other nodes, which then merge the remote state with their local state.
We will trigger the replication during this “TCP Push/Pull” process.
We defined a node state as: the set of last known version of other nodes.
For example:
{
"node_id": "flowg-0",
"last_sync": {
"flowg-1": {
"auth": 1,
"config": 2,
"log": 324
},
"flowg-2": {
"auth": 0,
"config": 0,
"log": 0
}
}
}
When
flowg-1
receives this state from
flowg-0
, it will start an HTTP request to
flowg-0
’s management interface and run (in parallel):
// POST http://<remote>/cluster/sync/auth
newAuthSince, err := authDb.Backup(
syncAuthRequestBodyWriter,
remoteState.LastSync["flowg-1"].Auth,
)
// send `X-FlowG-Since: <newAuthSince>` as HTTP trailer
// POST http://<remote>/cluster/sync/config
newConfigSince, err := configDb.Backup(
syncConfigRequestBodyWriter,
remoteState.LastSync["flowg-1"].Config,
)
// send `X-FlowG-Since: <newConfigSince>` as HTTP trailer
// POST http://<remote>/cluster/sync/log
newLogSince, err := logDb.Backup(
syncLogRequestBodyWriter,
remoteState.LastSync["flowg-1"].Log,
)
// send `X-FlowG-Since: <newLogSince>` as HTTP trailer
On the node
flowg-0
, the HTTP handler for
/cluster/sync/...
will read the request body:
nodeId := request.Header.Get("X-FlowG-NodeID")
err := db.Load(syncLogrequestBodyReader, 1)
updateLocalState("log", nodeId, request.Trailer.Get("X-FlowG-Since"))
And voilà! We have actual replication.
A few considerations
This is only a draft, and it is still highly experimental. Without further testing to understand:
what happens if the syncing fails?
what happens during a network partition?
what happens if a node fails?
…
I would not recommend going to production. But you’re free to test and open bug reports:
Issues · link-society/flowg
Low Code / Visual Scriptin

data.author: voxadam

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在放射学和病理学领域的应用前景及其实际效果

不同观点：
• Workaccount2认为，当前文章中对"AI"的描述过于宽泛，混淆了不同AI架构的能力。他指出，文中的AI示例使用的是较为陈旧的CNN架构，而更大规模的Transformer模型可能会表现出色。他质疑本地运行的CNN模型是否能与大规模Transformer模型媲美。
• Pseudocomposer分享了自己在AI病理算法集成方面的工作经验，认为AI工具可以提高病理学家的工作效率，并带来显著的经济效益。然而，市场对这种方法的价值认同度不高。
• Joshdavham指出，非领域专家常自信地断言AI将取代某些专业领域，但这种观点可能缺乏对实际复杂性的理解。
• Seesthruya是一位有20年经验的放射科医生，他认为AI不会在五年内取代人类放射科医生，并对自己的职业前景持乐观态度。
• Epistasis提到，一些在病理学AI领域工作了约十年的创业公司，发现最有前景的市场是大型制药公司的研发部门，而不是医院或诊断实验室。
• Kazinator认为，需要持证上岗的职业不会轻易被AI取代。AI技术可以帮助标记医学诊断图像中人类可能忽略的细节，但最终仍需放射科医生解读。
• D_burfoot指出，LLM的强大在于可以从大量未标记文本中学习，但在医学图像领域，缺乏足够大的数据库。要“攻克”放射学，AI公司需要启动大规模的数据收集项目。
• EcommerceFlow质疑，当前的数据集是否是限制AI在放射学领域发展的主要因素，并提出如果发生大规模医疗数据泄露，是否会推动该领域的发展。
• Pj_mukh引用数据，指出自Hinton的预言以来，放射科医生数量增长了55%，质疑他其他预言的准确性。
• Airstrike幽默地问道，AI是否会降低X光检查的费用。
• Bobowzki指出，ML在放射学中的优势在于计算机可以同时观察传感器的整个动态范围，而人类只能观察窗口或压缩窗口。
• Jmward01认为，神经网络在模式识别方面表现出色，阻碍其在放射学中应用的主要因素是电子健康记录提供商、法规以及行业的惯性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及AI在放射学和病理学中的具体应用、技术限制、市场接受度以及伦理和法律问题。
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否能在短期内取代或显著辅助放射科医生，以及当前的技术和数据是否足够支持这一进程。
• 不同观点中对AI能力的评价和对市场接受度的看法存在显著差异，反映出技术发展与实际应用之间的差距。

• Joshdavham指出，非领域专家常自信地断言AI将取代某些专业领域，但这种观点可能缺乏对实际复杂性的理解。
• Seesthruya是一位有20年经验的放射科医生，他认为AI不会在五年内取代人类放射科医生，并对自己的职业前景持乐观态度。
• Epistasis提到，一些在病理学AI领域工作了约十年的创业公司，发现最有前景的市场是大型制药公司的研发部门，而不是医院或诊断实验室。
• Kazinator认为，需要持证上岗的职业不会轻易被AI取代。AI技术可以帮助标记医学诊断图像中人类可能忽略的细节，但最终仍需放射科医生解读。
• D_burfoot指出，LLM的强大在于可以从大量未标记文本中学习，但在医学图像领域，缺乏足够大的数据库。要“攻克”放射学，AI公司需要启动大规模的数据收集项目。
• EcommerceFlow质疑，当前的数据集是否是限制AI在放射学领域发展的主要因素，并提出如果发生大规模医疗数据泄露，是否会推动该领域的发展。
• Pj_mukh引用数据，指出自Hinton的预言以来，放射科医生数量增长了55%，质疑他其他预言的准确性。
• Airstrike幽默地问道，AI是否会降低X光检查的费用。
• Bobowzki指出，ML在放射学中的优势在于计算机可以同时观察传感器的整个动态范围，而人类只能观察窗口或压缩窗口。
• Jmward01认为，神经网络在模式识别方面表现出色，阻碍其在放射学中应用的主要因素是电子健康记录提供商、法规以及行业的惯性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及AI在放射学和病理学中的具体应用、技术限制、市场接受度以及伦理和法律问题。
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否能在短期内取代或显著辅助放射科医生，以及当前的技术和数据是否足够支持这一进程。
• 不同观点中对AI能力的评价和对市场接受度的看法存在显著差异，反映出技术发展与实际应用之间的差距。

• [user9999999999] 提出优先考虑种植树木而非道路建设，暗示支持绿色基础设施而不是一味扩展交通网络。
• [jaoane] 对通过限制汽车使用来增加流动性的建议表示讽刺，认为这种做法实际上是让人们更不方便拥有汽车，从而质疑其有效性。

data.title: Robot chefs take over at South Korea's highway restaurants, to mixed reviews
data.author: NDAjam
data.article_summary: 文章报道了韩国一些高速公路餐厅正用机器人厨师取代人类厨师，以解决劳动力短缺问题。这些机器人由科技公司开发，能够在短时间内制作大量餐食，如拉面和乌冬面，效率远超人类厨师。然而， former厨师们表示，他们的角色被降级为清洁工，失去了对烹饪的自豪感。顾客也对机器人制作的食品质量表示不满，认为不如以前的美味。尽管机器人提高了效率，但也引发了人力劳动的减少和员工尊严的丧失。韩国计划到2030年增加至100万台机器人，以应对老龄化社会的劳动力短缺问题。文章通过Munmak休息站的例子，展示了自动化在服务业中的应用和影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自动化对不同行业的影响以及未来人类工作的形态

不同观点：
• nialse认为自动化正在进入新的领域，如烹饪和认知工作，未来这种趋势会在更多行业出现。自动化背景下，人类工作将更多地转向监督和支持自动化过程。
• alnwlsn通过历史案例AMFare系统指出，类似的自动化尝试（如60年代的快餐自动化）并未成功，且存在维护困难的问题。这暗示对当前自动化趋势可能面临相似挑战的担忧。
• potato3732842将自动化引发的抱怨类比为商业扩展中因雇佣下属而导致质量变化的常见问题，暗示自动化带来的不满可能与传统的管理问题类似。
• djmips预测未来卡车司机等职业也会被机器人取代，强调自动化对就业市场的全面影响。
• logic_node支持一种混合方法，认为机器人可以处理重复性任务，而人类厨师则专注于创造性和保持菜肴的文化本质。这种方法可以在技术进步和保护传统之间取得平衡。

43984505.article_content:
Photography by Jun Michael Park for Rest of World
By
Michelle Kim
14 May 2025
• Gangwon-do, South Korea
Robot chefs are replacing humans at some South Korean highway restaurants.
Tech companies say robots can help solve labor shortage in an aging nation.
Workers say their roles have been downgraded from chefs to cleaning staff.
On sweltering summer days, chef Park Jeong-eun would cook
makguksu
, an earthy Korean dish made with buckwheat noodles steeped in a tangy, ice-cold broth, topped with spicy gochujang paste. Truck drivers would come from faraway places to the Munmak rest stop, on the highway in the mountainous Gangwon-do province in South Korea, to eat her food.
That was until February 2024, when three robot chefs took over the kitchen at Munmak. The restaurant’s menu has since changed, away from local delicacies like
makguksu
and slow-cooked beef stews to easily automatable dishes such as ramen, udon, and varieties of Korean stews. The robots speed through 150 meals every hour, nearly double what Park can make by hand.
A “robot barista” is out of service while drivers take a break at Munmak Service Area in Gangwon Province.
Lee Hyeon works in collaboration with a robot at Munmak Service Area.
Jun Michael Park for Rest of World
When longtime patrons learn their beloved menu items are no more, they gasp and walk out the door, she recalled to
Rest of World
.
“Our customers say the dishes we used to cook tasted much better than what the robots serve now,” Park, 58, said. “Even though the robots have lightened my workload, I’ve lost my sense of pride in our food.”
Park now finds refuge scrubbing dishes in the back of the kitchen, away from the counter, where customers barrage her with harsh complaints about the food. Sometimes, they return their ramen bowls untouched in protest, she said.
The robot chefs at Munmak are part of South Korea’s push toward greater automation in the service sector. The nation already leads the world in
industrial robots
, with more than 1,000 machines for every 10,000 workers in 2023, nearly three times the global average.
South Korean tech companies are now deploying collaborative robots, or co-bots, which work alongside humans, in hotels, elder care, schools, and restaurants. The sector is projected to reach
$367 million
in value this year, from $254 million in 2024, according to the Korea Institute of Science and Technology Information.
The bots are supposed to solve a looming labor shortage in the rapidly aging nation, where workers aged 60 and above make up nearly
a quarter
of the workforce. The government
plans
to increase the number of bot workers to 1 million by 2030 as a longterm solution.
Munmak, too, faced a severe work shortage, and bot chefs help keep the kitchen staffed 24/7, Ham Jin-kyu, president of the Korea Expressway Corporation, a public institution that manages the country’s rest stops, said during Munmak’s grand reopening last year.
Although some aspects of daily restaurant operations have been automated, they still require significant human labor.
“For tasks too demanding for humans to perform 24 hours a day, we need to use robots in a limited capacity, in this transformative era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution,” Ham said, referring to the current wave of automation across industries.
Human chefs who work alongside the robot chefs told
Rest of World
they are able to work at a more relaxed pace, especially during peak hours, because the machines grind away tirelessly. But they also spoke of layoffs and a loss of dignity due to automation.
Some of the kitchen staff even quit because they couldn’t get used to the menial nature of working alongside the robots.
Munmak sits on the Yeongdong highway, conveniently located as a stop for freight trucks, charter buses, and cars dashing to the countryside.
Inside the “smart” rest stop, machines whir quietly. A truckers’ lounge offers an electric massage bed. There’s a self-service convenience store, and Cafe Hubot, where a robot barista brews coffee behind a plexiglass counter. And then there’s the automated restaurant.
When a customer orders a bowl of dumpling ramen at a kiosk, a robot activates. A steel nozzle swirls boiling water and spicy broth paste into a pot. Dried noodles drop from a dispenser. Cradling heat and spice, the pot glides onto a burner. An overhead chute sprinkles dried vegetable flakes. The ramen simmers.
Finally, a kitchen worker stirs the noodles and places a few dumplings on top. A robotic arm lifts the pot and pours the ramen into a bowl, which travels down a conveyor belt to the counter.
“Customer number 477, your food is ready,” an automated voice announces to a catchy tune.
The robots were developed by Chef Robot Tech, a startup based in Namyangju, a robotics hub outside Seoul. The company reprogrammed the RB5 co-bot, originally built by a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, to mimic human cooking motions. They used training data created from dozens of trial runs by a team of engineers

data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: ESP WebRTC Solution v1.0 是专为轻量级嵌入式设备设计的稳定版本，支持 ESP32 系列芯片上的实时音视频通信。该方案提供了高层次的 API（esp_webrtc），简化了 WebRTC 应用开发，支持点对点媒体与数据通信、灵活的信令机制（如 AppRTC、WHIP、OpenAI Realtime 等），以及音视频编解码器（如 H.264、OPUS、G.711 等）。此外，方案具有低内存消耗，并提供了多个演示项目，如门铃、OpenAI 聊天机器人、WHIP 发布等。该版本兼容 ESP32、ESP32-S2、ESP32-S3、ESP32-P4 芯片，推荐使用 ESP-IDF v5.4 或更高版本。
data.comments_summary:

• 有人可能隐含认为这些应用只是“有趣”或娱乐性质的，并没有深入探讨其更深层次的潜力或实用价值，但并未直接表达负面观点。

• Sean-Der提到了一个具体实例：有人在X平台上展示通过语音输入控制小车的视频，这说明WebRTC和AI结合在实时通信和硬件控制方面已经取得了一些实际成果。
• 该评论还暗示了WebRTC在实时处理和应用中的重要性，特别是在与AI结合时，可以实现复杂的功能，如语音识别和硬件控制。
• 未有直接的争议，但潜在的讨论可能围绕这种技术应用的广泛性和实用性展开，例如是否仅限于娱乐，还是在更广泛的领域有应用潜力。

Overview
ESP WebRTC Solution v1.0
is the first
stable release
of Espressif’s WebRTC implementation designed specifically for
lightweight embedded devices
. This version delivers a comprehensive protocol stack for building
real-time communication applications
on
ESP32 series chips
, supporting
audio/video streaming
,
data channel communication
, and
customizable signaling mechanisms
.
🚀 Highlights
High-level
esp_webrtc
API for easy WebRTC application development
Support for peer-to-peer media and data communication via RTP and SCTP
TURN support, NACK handling, SCTP SACK support
Flexible signaling abstraction with built-in support for AppRTC, WHIP, OpenAI Realtime, and local HTTP SSE
Audio/video capture and rendering modules with codec abstraction
Out-of-the-box support for key audio/video codecs: H.264, MJPEG, OPUS, G.711, AAC
Demo projects for
doorbell
,
OpenAI chatbot
,
WHIP
publishing, and more
Fewer dependencies
(only depends on
libSRTP
; all other modules are included in
ESP-IDF
)
Lightweight and low memory consumption
— designed specifically for embedded devices
1. Core WebRTC Components
1.1 High-level
esp_webrtc
API
The
esp_webrtc
API internally manages PeerConnection state and signaling flow, making it easy to build WebRTC applications. In most cases, users only need to adapt it to their custom board and signaling — everything else is handled by
esp_webrtc
.
1.2 WebRTC Peer Connection (
esp_peer
)
esp_peer
abstracts WebRTC PeerConnection logic on ESP32 devices and includes a default implementation (
peer_default
) derived from
libpeer
, with the following features:
Full TURN support (RFC5766 and RFC8656)
Optimized connection speed with multiple ICE candidates
Supports both Controlling and Controlled roles
RTP NACK support for retransmission
SCTP SACK support for large data transmission
Separate tasks for sending/receiving to avoid blocking
Codec support:
Video
: H.264 (baseline), MJPEG (data channel only)
Audio
: G.711 (PCMA/PCMU), OPUS
1.3 WebRTC Signaling (
esp_peer_signaling
)
Signaling is used to detect peers and exchange SDP/control commands.
esp_peer_signaling
abstracts signaling logic, allowing easy integration of custom signaling without modifying the core WebRTC stack. Built-in implementations:
esp_signaling_get_apprtc_impl
: AppRTC signaling via WebSocket
esp_signaling_get_whip_impl
: WHIP protocol for publishing to WebRTC servers
esp_signaling_get_openai_signaling
: OpenAI Realtime API for chatbot integration
esp_signaling_get_http_impl
: Local signaling via HTTP SSE for testing
2. Media Provider
2.1 Media Capture (
esp_capture
)
Integrated audio/video capture framework supporting various devices and codecs:
Video
: H.264 (baseline), MJPEG
Audio
: G.711 (PCMA/PCMU), AAC, OPUS
Capture device abstraction allows plug-and-play development:
esp_capture_new_audio_codec_src
: I2S audio (via
esp_codec_dev
)
esp_capture_new_audio_aec_src
: I2S audio with AEC
esp_capture_new_video_v4l2_src
: V4L2 (MIPI CSI/DVP, ESP32-P4 only)
esp_capture_new_video_dvp_src
: DVP camera (ESP32-S3 and others)
2.2 Media Player (
av_render
)
A lightweight media player supporting a "push" model for playback:
Video
: H.264 (baseline), MJPEG
Audio
: G.711 (PCMA/PCMU), AAC, OPUS
Rendering device abstraction:
av_render_alloc_i2s_render
: Audio playback via I2S
av_render_alloc_lcd_render
: Video output via
esp_lcd
3. Board Configuration (
codec_board
)
Provides default configuration to simplify adapting audio boards for quick testing and verification.
4. Demo Solutions
Peer Demo
: Peer-to-peer demo between two ESP32 devices
Audio and data channel communication
OpenAI Demo
